items.title: Trump’s Affection for Russia Is No Mystery
items.description: A large majority of the Republican Party, including many officials who initially viewed Donald Trump with deep skepticism, decided early in Trump’s first term that the investigations into Russian interference in the 2016 election were the hysterical product of Trump Derangement Syndrome in the Deep State and the media. There was no mystery to solve, no scandal to uncover, in Trump’s affinity for Vladimir Putin. And yet this strange alliance continues to bedevil American foreign policy. On Friday afternoon, Trump announced that he had held another call with Putin, and came away once again depicting the Russian dictator as a cherished friend to whom he owes a great deal. “I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter,” he wrote on Truth Social. Later that day, Trump reemphasized his debt of gratitude. “I want to thank President Putin, to be honest with you. We have massive amounts of oil coming into our country, and it’s diesel, which is what we want. So, thank you,” he told reporters outside the White House. [ Read: Why is Kash Patel planning to visit Russia? ] Many of Trump’s comments make little sense, and these were no exception. But he was using a particular kind of illogic that conflicts with his standard brand of nonsense. Trump typically depicts international trade in starkly mercantilist terms. Exports, in his mind, are a form of profit, and imports are a loss. Trump sees trade deficits as a form of theft, and conceives of a “good deal” as one in which the United States reduces its imports or increases its exports. This holds true of all goods, including oil. “We don’t need their fuel, we don’t need their energy, we don’t need their oil and gas. We don’t need anything that they have,” Trump said dismissively of Canada last year. Yet when it comes to imports from Russia, Trump inverts his standard accounting methods. He presents Russian oil as a kind of gift, something Putin plans to “supply.” (A more accurate verb to describe this transaction would be sell .) In reality, diesel fuel exists in a global market, and adding a small amount of Russian diesel into this enormous international supply would have a barely detectable effect upon its price. A more important effect would be on the Russian economy. Economic sanctions have hampered its ability to attract foreign currency, and the Trump-Putin plan would suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Doing so would in fact appear to violate American law, which prohibits importing oil from Russia unless it makes peace with Ukraine, though illegality does not usually deter Trump. The most immediate outcome of this plan has been to present Ukraine as the cause of economic turmoil and Russia as the innocent victim of Ukrainian warmongering. Trump almost immediately began to praise Putin and assail the Russian dictator’s adversary. Volodymyr Zelensky “could have settled this war many times—many, many times—and he chooses not to,” Trump told reporters on Friday outside the White House. “He wants to make problems for the world. He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel, because Russia supplies a large portion of the diesel fuel throughout the world.” Trump’s solution? “I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal. Because they could have made many deals, and for some reason, he never does.” There is no universally agreed-upon explanation for why Trump has remained so consistently faithful to Putin. One theory holds that Putin masterfully strokes Trump’s ego. Although Trump does respond to flattery, the flaw in this hypothesis is that other leaders have tried, and often failed, to mimic this formula. Europeans have met Trump’s second term with obsequious displays and gifts. Ukraine floated a proposal to rename the Donbas region “Donnyland.” Poland proposed christening a base “Fort Trump.” Yet these countries have remained largely frustrated. A second theory holds that Trump simply admires dictators. This one contains a bit more truth, as seen by Trump’s swooning over Xi Jinping and even Kim Jong Un. But the dictators running Iran and Venezuela have hardly managed to duplicate the Trump-Putin partnership. A third theory depicts Trump as merely amoral, driven by transactions and indifferent to moral concerns. Yet he has continued to defer to Putin even as the Russian dictator has undermined Trump’s own standing by aiding Iran in its war with the United States. Meanwhile, Zelensky’s assistance against Iran seems to have bought him no goodwill whatsoever. Trump’s view of the war is moralistic—he simply blames the victim rather than the aggressor. “You don’t start a war against someone 20 times your size and then hope that people give you some missiles,” he said last year of Zelensky. Explaining the depth of Trump’s identification with Putin may require looking at a possibility that conservatives have been dismissing out of hand for a decade: manipulation and corruption. During the 2016 campaign, Russia dangled a lucrative deal to develop Trump-branded properties in Russia that would deliver hundreds of millions of dollars in profit with no risk. More recently, The New York Times reported that Trump advisers and Russian officials have floated deals that would enrich Trump’s inner circle as part of ending the war. Russia has tried to bribe foreign officials, especially by handing out pieces of its resource wealth, in numerous countries. It would be strange if Putin didn’t try to replicate this tried-and-true method in the United States. [ Anne Applebaum: Trump’s message to Ukraine is now crystal clear ] Perhaps the best evidence against corruption is that Trump now has access to so many other sources of wealth that he hardly needs any financial incentive to tilt toward Russia. Yet Putin seems able to bring the American president around to his way of thinking, if not effortlessly (their most recent phone call reportedly consumed an hour and a half) then at least reliably. There is obviously no investigation at the moment into Putin’s efforts to influence American foreign policy. Instead, incredibly, we have an investigation into the Russia investigation. The Trump administration is working to gin up criminal charges against former CIA Director John Brennan, former FBI Director James Comey, and other American officials whose crime was to explore whether something fishy was going on between the Trump campaign and Moscow. My colleagues Jonathan Lemire and Simon Shuster report , “Some of Trump’s closest advisers have privately wondered what Putin has done to so thoroughly enthrall the president.” Perhaps instead of dismissing the people who were trying to shed light on this mystery and then attempting to throw them into prison, these advisers should be taking their concerns seriously.

items.title: El Vaticano revela que el Papa tenía un tumor maligno en el pulmón y la operación ha concluido “positivamente”
items.description: El Papa tenía un tumor maligno en el pulmón, según han confirmado los primeros análisis tras la operación a la que se ha sometido este martes y en la que le ha sido extirpado. Así lo ha hecho saber el Vaticano en un breve comunicado difundido a las 21.54. El primer parte médico ha señalado que la intervención ha durado hora y media, ha transcurrido sin complicaciones y ha consistido en la extracción del “lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho mediante una técnica asistida por video”. “El examen histológico intraoperatorio ha confirmado el diagnóstico de adenocarcinoma pulmonar, tal como se sospechaba a partir de las pruebas preoperatorias”, revela la nota. items.title: Atta Akyea denies seeking presidential pardon for Wontumi in galamsey case
items.description: Private legal practitioner Samuel Atta Akyea has denied formally seeking a presidential pardon for his client, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, in a galamsey-related case. Mr Atta Akyea dismissed suggestions that he had approached President John Dramani Mahama to secure clemency for the former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman. “No, please. We didn’t do that,” he said on Accra-based Citi FM on Tuesday, October 13, when asked whether he had sought a presidential pardon for his client. However, Mr Atta Akyea said he had expected President Mahama might consider granting Mr Boasiako a pardon, given the widespread nature of illegal mining in the country. He argued that the President could take into account the scale of galamsey and the involvement of influential individuals in the practice when considering cases related to illegal mining. “Also, when the case was galamsey-related, we thought that the president, in his own mercy, would say that, look, the nation is awash with galamsey,” he said. Mr Atta Akyea added that he had expected the President to be reluctant to impose a lengthy prison sentence in a case linked to illegal mining. “Even we have some evidence that serious people in the party- that is what their daily bread is all about. I will not use a galamsey-tinted criminal matter to detain a man and let him remain there for 20 years. I’ll grant him pardon,” he said, describing what he believed the President might do. His comments follow President Mahama’s decision on October 5 to grant presidential pardons to 863 convicted persons under Article 72(1) of the 1992 Constitution, following consultation with the Council of State. The pardons were announced as part of activities commemorating Ghana’s Independence Anniversary.

items.title: La Fondation Orange Guinée & ses partenaires – en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique ; le Ministère de la Femme, Famille et Solidarité – lancent le Programme Santé 3.0
items.description: Conakry, le 12 octobre 202 6- Le 7 octobre 2026 , aux côtés de ses partenaires et en présence des S ecrétaires G énéraux des deux départements ministériels , Dr Mory KEITA du MSHP et Mr Saa Kossa TOURE du MFFS, a été lancé le Programme Santé 3.0 , une initiative qui regroupe 11 acteurs mobilisés autour d’un seul objectif : agir en faveur de la santé et du bien-être des populations guinéennes. Le Programme Santé 3.0, fruit d’un partenariat public privé ambitieux , est un programme de santé pluridisciplinaire qui se traduit par une approche structurée , séquencée et durable . Il apporte des solutions concrètes aux défis enregistrés en matière d’accès aux soins de santé au sein des communautés, plus précisément sur des maladies évitables dont les statistiques disponibles indiquent une progression rapide en plus du rajeunissement et des taux de prévalence élevés chez les femmes. Les maladies ciblées par ce consortium sont : le diabète, l’hypertension artérielle, les maladies auditives, le cancer du col de l’utérus, le paludisme , la santé sexuelle et reproductive. L’initiative de la Fondation Orange Guinée porte l’ambition partagée des partenaires ci- après, tous engagés sur une mise en œuvre durant 3 ans : – Le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique à travers entre autres la Direction Nationale de la Promotion de la santé, la Direction de la santé Communautaire, la Direction Nationale de la Lutte contre la Maladie – Le Ministère de la F emme, F amille et Solidarité à travers la Direction Nationale des Personnes Vulnérables et celle du Fonds de Développement Social et de l’Indigence – Le Programme national de lutte contre les maladies non transmissibles (PNLMNT), – Le Programme national de lutte contre le paludisme (PNLP) , – Le Programme national de Lutte contre le Cancer (PNLC) – La Société Civile (CNOSCG) – L ’ Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) , – Le Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA) , – La Croix-Rouge Guinéenne (CRG) , – Sante en Entreprise – Santé Intégrée – Solthis , – Visa Médical et – Sanofi Tous unissent leurs expertises pour renforcer la prévention, le dépistage, la prise en charge et l’accès aux soins, notamment dans les zones décentralisées, au plus près des communautés. Le Programme Santé 3.0 se déploiera autour de trois leviers complémentaires : • La formation des agents de santé communautaires , afin de renforcer leurs capacités d’écoute, de prévention, d’orientation et d’accompagnement des patients ; • Le déploiement d’ une caravane mobile , proposant consultations, dépistage, conseils et orientation médicale dans les localités ciblées ; • La sensibilisation et prévention en continue, pour encourager la prévention, le dépistage précoce et le recours aux services de santé disponibles à proximité. C e lancement ouvre surtout une séquence de déploiement progressif avec le démarrage des formations dans les localités retenues précédent la 1ere caravane mobile M Ousmane Boly TRAORE , Président de la Fondation Orange Guinée confirmera d’ ailleurs « Avec le Programme Santé 3.0, nous franchissons une nouvelle étape de notre engagement en faveur du bien-être des Guinéens. Notre ambition est d’agir collectivement et dans la durée pour renforcer la prévention, le dépistage et l’accès aux soins, au plus près des populations. » Le Programme Santé 3.0 place l’humain au cœur de son action pour encore mieux accompagner les communautés , soutenir les agents de santé et les relais communautaires, et assurer un impact concret des actions menées sur le terrain. À travers cette initiative, 1ere en son genre en Guinée, à la fois le MSHP, le MFFS, la Fondation Orange Guinée et l’ensemble des partenaires engagés affirment leur volonté de faire de la santé de proximité une réalité forte d’une véritable coord ination garante d’une pérennité au service des guinéens et guinéennes. À propos de la Fondation Orange Guinée La Fondation Orange Guinée s’engage pour un accès égal à l’éducation, la santé et la culture. Ses programmes entendent contribuer à l’amélioration de la santé maternelle et infantile et la santé du 3 e âge ; au renforcement de l’employabilité des jeunes, l’autonomisation des femmes ; la réinsertion et employabilité des jeunes et la préservation du patrimoine culturel. Avec plus d’un million de personnes touchées par ses programmes, elle a pour ambition en 2024 de continuer à agir pour contribuer à la construction d’une société plus inclusive, une société dans laquelle le numérique est un des leviers incontournables du développement humain de chaque guinéen. En savoir plus : https://www.orange-guinee.com/fr/fondation.html L’article La Fondation Orange Guinée & ses partenaires – en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique ; le Ministère de la Femme, Famille et Solidarité – lancent le Programme Santé 3.0 est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Ex-gang leader sentenced to minimum 40 years for Tupac murder
items.description: Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former Los Angeles gang leader who boasted for years of his involvement in the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, only to deny it when he came to trial, was sentenced to a minimum 40 years in prison on Tuesday. The sentence, which will likely see him die in custody, comes three decades after the gunning down of one of the most influential hip hop artists of the late 20th century, and after years of criticism over investigations that went nowhere. Davis, 63, formerly ran a branch of the feared Crips, one of a patchwork of rival gangs that controlled parts of Los Angeles in the 1990s. He spent years evading justice and seemingly believed he was beyond the reach of the law when he wrote in his memoir that he had ordered the killing of Shakur. “For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing to law enforcement… in your book, and it’s something like, ‘Yeah, I was involved in this, but I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,'” Judge Carli Kierny told Davis as she handed down the sentence in a Las Vegas courtroom. “I’m here to tell you that’s not how this works.” “You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur,” the judge said. Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas. A trial heard how Davis ordered the September 7, 1996 killing of the hip-hop artist after his own nephew had been beaten by members of Shakur’s entourage at a Las Vegas casino. The “California Love” artist was shot about two hours after the casino confrontation by a gunman in a white Cadillac that pulled up at a red light alongside the BMW in which the rapper was riding. Davis handed the gun to someone sitting in the back seat of the Cadillac and ordered that person to shoot Shakur, who died six days later. The name of that person has not been definitively revealed and Davis is the only person who was in the Cadillac that evening who is still alive. The driver of the BMW, Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight, was wounded. – ‘Born an icon’ – The killing of Shakur, also known as 2Pac, was one of America’s most famous cold cases, prompting endless debate among music fans over who did it, and why. Known for hits including “All Eyez on Me,” Shakur — the son of a Black Panther activist — was raised in Harlem and Baltimore, but quickly became the epitome of California hip hop when he signed with Los Angeles-based Death Row Records. His sister Sekyiwa Shakur paid emotional tribute on Tuesday to her brother, a man whom she said “was born an icon.” She said their mother “consciously raised him to be a human rights activist, someone to stand up for those weaker and smaller than he was, and that’s who he was to me and all the family. He was the person that you go to for protection. “He dedicated his career to the advancement of his people. He was gentle and kind to women and children. He fed anyone he knew that didn’t have. He was truly my shining star, my shining prince. He was who God trusted to take care of me.” Davis offered no words of contrition ahead of the sentence being handed down, vowing only to appeal the guilty finding. items.title: Photos: Mahama commissions 85-bed Police Hospital ward, donates two ambulances
items.description: President John Mahama has commended the Ghana Police Service for improvements in public safety and crime investigations, while urging the Service to sustain efforts to protect lives and property. He made the remarks on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at the commissioning of a new 85-bed ward complex at the Ghana Police Hospital in Accra. The facility, named the Christian Tetteh Yohuno Ward Complex after the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), is expected to improve healthcare for police personnel, their families and the general public. The President praised IGP Christian Tetteh Yohuno and the Police Administration for their work in maintaining peace and security across the country. He said investment in police healthcare was essential because officers regularly face physical and psychological demands in the line of duty, including exposure to violence, emergencies and other traumatic situations. President Mahama stressed that officers injured during operations must receive timely and quality medical care, adding that their welfare was closely linked to their ability to protect the public effectively. He urged the hospital’s management and staff to maintain high standards of hygiene, patient safety and professional care, while ensuring that the new facility and its equipment were properly maintained. To strengthen emergency response and patient care, the President also donated two new ambulances to the hospital. He further assured the Police Service of additional logistical support, including more armoured vehicles, as part of efforts to improve operational effectiveness and officer safety. The commissioning forms part of efforts to expand the Police Hospital’s capacity to serve both security personnel and the wider public. Inspector-General of Police Christian Tetteh Yohuno welcomed the new facility, describing it as an important step towards improving healthcare delivery for officers, their families and other patients. He said the additional beds and expanded facilities would enable the hospital to provide more specialised care on site, reducing the need to transfer patients to other health facilities and easing the associated costs and inconvenience. The IGP reaffirmed the Police Administration’s commitment to maintaining the complex and ensuring that it continued to provide quality healthcare to all who needed its services.

items.title: GTEC directs Ghana’s public universities to reopen by October 16 and begin lectures on October 19
items.description: The Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) has directed all public universities to reopen their campuses for the 2026/2027 academic year by Friday, October 16, despite any earlier decisions to postpone reopening. In a letter dated October 13, 2026, and signed by Deputy Director-General Prof. Augustine Ocloo on behalf of the Director-General, the Commission said academic activities, particularly lectures, must commence on Monday, October 19. The directive was issued on the authority of the Minister for Education. GTEC has also directed university managements to ensure that halls of residence, academic libraries, departmental registration desks and other essential student support facilities are fully staffed and operational by Thursday, October 15. Vice-Chancellors are required to submit comprehensive academic reopening readiness reports to the Commission by Wednesday, October 14. The directive comes amid an industrial dispute involving the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) and the Technical University Administrators Association of Ghana (TUSAAG). GTEC acknowledged the administrative challenges arising from the industrial action but warned that the continued suspension of academic activities had far-reaching implications for students’ academic progression, university operations, tertiary education delivery and international academic partnerships. The Commission said the government, through the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Finance and Fair Wages and Salaries Commission, had initiated engagements with GAUA’s leadership to facilitate the resolution of outstanding grievances. It has asked members of GAUA to resume their administrative duties while good-faith negotiations continue. “The Commission expects strict compliance with the stipulated timelines,” the letter stated. GTEC further directed institutions that anticipate difficulties meeting the deadlines to notify the Commission immediately in writing, outlining the challenges and measures being taken to address them. The directive follows a meeting between Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu and the leadership of GAUA and TUSAAG on Monday, October 12, during which the Minister expressed optimism that the strike would be called off in the coming days. GAUA, however, said it needed to consult its members before announcing a decision. The industrial action, which began on August 10 and was reactivated on September 15, centres on disparities in the Interim Market Premium (IMP) between teaching and non-teaching senior members. The strike has disrupted administrative operations at public universities, including admissions, registration and accommodation allocation. The University of Ghana and Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) have postponed their reopenings indefinitely. Under the latest directive, universities are expected to reopen by October 16 and begin lectures three days later, while negotiations over the outstanding grievances continue. items.title: 2027: Hamzat unveils policy agenda, promises reforms in transport, housing, security
items.description: The Deputy Gov. of Lagos State, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, has unveiled a policy agenda for the state, promising reforms in transportation, housing, security, technology, food distribution and justice delivery ahead of the 2027 governorship election. Hamzat made the commitments while presenting his Promise Agenda, tagged, ‘An Afternoon to Discuss the Facts and Figures of Lagos State: The 8th Largest Economy in Africa’. The event was organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) in collaboration with the Contact and Mobilisation Committee, Formal Sector for PBAT and KOH on Tuesday in Victoria Island, Lagos State. . Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 elections, described it as a social contract with Lagos residents, which he pledged to implement from May 29, 2027, if elected governor. He said the agenda was designed to establish measurable targets for government, enabling residents to assess performance and hold the administration accountable for its promises. Hamzat said transportation remained one of Lagos most pressing challenges, noting that traffic congestion costs the state an estimated economic losses of N1 trillion annually, with residents spending an average of four hours daily in traffic. He said Lagos had a vehicle density of 212 vehicles per kilometre, compared with the national average of 16, making the development of alternative transportation systems imperative. According to him, the state has identified 63 traffic junctions for improvement and addressed 33 of them, while plans are underway to expand Bus Rapid Transit services, improve terminals, develop rail infrastructure and increase water transportation. He said his administration would prioritise waterways to reduce pressure on roads, including developing ferry terminals and improving connections between communities such as Ikorodu, Badagry and other parts of Lagos. Hamzat also promised improved pedestrian walkways, greener public spaces and better organised bus terminals to separate commuters from vehicular traffic. He said the state aimed to plant 10 million trees within four years. On water supply, Hamzat said the completion of an ongoing water infrastructure project would provide additional access to water for six million people. On Jobs, technology and business growth, the APC candidate said the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund had supported businesses and activated about 340,000 jobs since 2019. He added that his administration if elected, would strengthen mentorship and business management support to help small enterprises survive and expand. He said the state had proposed four industrial parks in Epe, Badagry, Ikorodu and Ojo under its 2025–2030 industrial policy. Hamzat also pledged to harmonise government levies and regulatory processes to reduce the burden on businesses, while reviewing charges imposed on petty traders and micro-enterprises. On technology, he described Yaba as a major technology hub, saying its technology ecosystem had developed into a 15.3-billion-dollar economy with about 2,000 start-ups. He noted that Lagos was implementing a 1,000-kilometre fibre-optic cable network, with plans to expand it to 6,000 kilometres, while reducing broadband costs and supporting local technology companies. The deputy governor further added that the state would adopt a local-first procurement approach by giving qualified Nigerian technology firms the first opportunity to supply products required by the government. On food security and creative economy, Hamzat said the state was developing a 420-hectare food logistics hub and cold-chain network to reduce food wastage, improve storage and cut transportation costs between farmers and markets. He said: “The cold-chain facilities in Mushin and Gbagada has helped market women reduce logistics costs by 40 per cent while government is expanding medium-scale markets across the state.” “Also, the state will support farmers through a proposed N500 billion guarantee scheme, alongside arrangements in facilitating the purchase and distribution of locally produced food.” On the creative industry, Hamzat said Lagos would strengthen training in contract negotiation and intellectual property to enable artists and other creative professionals to earn better returns from their work. On Justice, inclusion and social welfare, the APC governorship candidate said the state was working with the judiciary to increase the civil jurisdiction of magistrates courts from N10 million to N15 million to reduce the backlog of cases in the High Courts. He said the government also wanted landlord-tenant disputes resolved within three months, adding that more courts would be established to improve access to justice. He disclosed that about 198 people had been prosecuted for domestic violence, stressing the need to strengthen support for survivors and encourage more victims to seek justice. On inclusion, Hamzat said women-led enterprises performed well among small businesses, adding that the government planned to allocate five per cent of its business support to women-led enterprises. He also promised to certify artisans and other skilled workers in their preferred languages and establish an online platform where customers could assess their services through reviews. He said the government would pay 40 per cent of the stipends of trainees placed in companies under its vocational and technical training programmes to encourage businesses to employ them. Hamzat added that the state would strengthen child protection by ensuring that children below 18 years were either in school or acquiring vocational skills. On security, he said Lagos had about 6,800 personnel in its safety agency and was recruiting an additional 2,500, adding that the personnel could form a foundation for state policing if the necessary constitutional approval was secured. He said the state had increased insurance benefits for police officers who died in service to N4 million for junior officers and N10 million for senior officers, stressing the need to improve support for their families. Hamzat also called for stronger climate adaptation measures, including improved drainage, community protection and early-warning systems to prepare residents for extreme rainfall and flooding. On housing, the deputy governor said the state would collaborate with private developers to increase the supply of affordable homes, noting that the average period for an African to build a house was about 17 years. According to him, we will explore housing and mortgage arrangements that enabled young people and low-income earners to secure decent accommodation without sacrificing other basic needs. Hamzat said the commitments would be assessed against measurable targets to ensure accountability, adding that government, businesses and residents must work together to achieve a more inclusive and prosperous Lagos. Earlier, the LCCI President, Mr Leye Kupoluyi, stated that the engagement provided an opportunity for the business community to assess the economic policies and development priorities of prospective political leaders. He said: “it gives us direct impact of government policies on investment, operating costs and business growth.” Kupoluyi identified five key priority areas for the next administration, which included reducing the cost of doing business, improving infrastructure and mobility, reforming the tax and regulatory framework, promoting economic growth and investment, and empowering small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs). He said addressing high energy and logistics costs, traffic congestion, freight bottlenecks and regulatory challenges would improve productivity and create a more conducive business environment. The LCCI president also called for improved access to capital, technology and markets for SMEs, emphasising the need for stronger collaboration between government and the private sector to unlock Lagos State economic potential. He reaffirmed the Chamber’s commitment to constructive, evidence-based engagement with political leaders and future administrations. The LCCI Deputy President, Mr Knit Ulvmoen, emphasised the need to strengthen local manufacturing and reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported finished goods. He noted that the country had the people, market and raw materials required to produce more goods locally. He cited the transformation of Nigeria’s cement industry from heavy reliance on imports to local production and exports as evidence of the benefits of adding value to domestic resources. Ulvmoen called for greater investment in sectors such as agriculture, pharmaceuticals, textiles, petrochemicals and renewable energy, while stressing that education and skills development are essential to preparing Nigerians for industrial growth and economic self-sufficiency. In his goodwill message, the Managing Director of Sterling Bank, Mr Abubakar Suleiman, identified Lagos State real estate sector as a major untapped source of capital. Suleiman urged the government to make land assets more accessible to investors through funding. He added that Lagos possessed a unique economic advantage as a financial hub, with substantial lending and investment activities already concentrated in the state. According to him, unlocking real estate value can significantly expand development funding. “If the government can do this, I am confident that the initiative could attract more domestic investment, boost development and strengthen Lagos ambition to become a leading global financial centre,” he said. items.title: Star Oil donates GH¢1million towards construction of new CID facility
items.description: Oil marketing company Star Oil has donated GH¢1 million to support the construction of a new facility for the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service. The new facility, estimated at GH¢11 million, is expected to improve the CID’s investigative and operational functions when completed. The project will provide office accommodation, interrogation rooms, and detention facilities for the department. Chief Executive Officer of Star Oil, Philip Tieku, said the donation was in recognition of the CID’s contribution to addressing security challenges facing the company’s nationwide operations. He noted how the Department’s work has helped Star Oil improve security monitoring at its more than 280 locations across the country, explaining that this has reduced the need for physical security personnel at some lower-risk stations. “The CID has been very supportive in that effort. They’ve assisted us in almost every situation that comes up, and we’ve gotten to the point where that collaboration has allowed us to operate a remote security monitoring system supported by the CID,” he said. Mr. Tieku added that the company considered it important to support the department’s infrastructure needs, having benefited from its services over the years. Receiving the donation, Director-General of the CID, COP Lydia Yaako Donkor, said the new facility would address longstanding challenges associated with the department’s lack of adequate detention space at its headquarters. She explained that the department often has to rely on other police stations for the detention and interrogation of arrested persons, placing additional pressure on those facilities. “For a while now, we’ve not had that facility within this headquarters, and it is also a matter of concern for us. We have to be sending people to other stations, and those stations are also burdened,” she said. The contractor for the project, David Mawuli of Delta Plus, said the facility will include eight detention cells for male and female suspects, as well as a separate cell for juveniles. The building will also accommodate interrogation rooms, investigation offices, and IT facilities, with a cafeteria planned for the top floor. Construction is expected to take 12 months, provided the required resources are made available.

items.title: Algérie : l’exécution de la peine de mort officiellement en vigueur
items.description: Le rétablissement de l’exécution de la peine de mort en Algérie a franchi ce mardi 13 octobre la dernière étape pour son entrée en vigueur avec la publication au Journal officiel de la Loi n° 26-13 du 12 octobre 2026 modifiant et complétant l’ordonnance n° 66-156 du 8 juin 1966 portant Code pénal. L’article 91 de cette Loi dispose que « quiconque enlève un enfant par tout moyen que ce soit, le torture, l’agresse sexuellement et/ou le mutile, nonobstant toute autre peine contraire prévue dans la législation en vigueur » est puni de la peine de mort . La personne condamnée pour l’un des faits réprimés par cet article, ne « bénéficie pas des circonstances atténuantes » prévues dans le code pénal. L’article 395 bis du nouveau Code pénal précise qu’il est « puni de la peine de mort, quiconque met « volontairement le feu à des forêts, bois ou champs plantés ou non, arbres, ou sections de bois, ou à des bois disposés en tas ou en stères à l’intérieur des forêts. ». L’Algérie rétablit officiellement l’exécution de la peine de mort Il est également puni de la peine de mort quiconque qui met « volontairement le feu à des biens qu’ils soient publics ou privés, sur incitation ou au profit d’un État étranger ou une partie étrangère ou dans le cadre des infractions de trahison et d’intelligence avec un État étranger, ou dans le cadre d’un groupe criminel organisé, ou si ces actes visent la sécurité et l'ordre publics, l'unité nationale, la stabilité des institutions et leur fonctionnement normal, l’économie nationale ou causent des dégâts à l'environnement, à l'équilibre écologique, aux ressources forestières, végétales, animales ou agricoles. » (Article 396 bis 1). Enfin, quiconque « incite à la commission des actes prévus aux articles 395 bis et 396 bis 1 du présent code, les encourage, les finance, les organise ou participe à leur commission, préparation ou facilitation par quelque moyen que ce soit, y compris par les technologies de l’information et de la communication et les réseaux sociaux » est aussi puni de la peine de mort. L’article Algérie : l’exécution de la peine de mort officiellement en vigueur est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes oil site in Yemen's capital
items.description: Yemen’s Houthis said Saudi Arabia struck an oil facility in Sanaa on Tuesday, after the Riyadh-led coalition told civilians to leave the surrounding area in its first evacuation order for the Yemeni capital since the war flared up again. The Saudi-led coalition said military operations were conducted against “vital assets” used by the Houthis to wage war in Yemen. In a statement posted on X, coalition spokesperson Major General Turki Al-Maliki says the targets included the Al-Sabaha central station in the capital Sanaa, underground fuel reserves and fuel tanks, and energy terminals in Hodeidah, Sanaa and Dhamar. Earlier, the coalition’s spokesman said people should leave an oil facility belonging to the Yemen Petroleum Company on the western outskirts of Sanaa before it was attacked. An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported hearing an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said, “Saudi aggression targets the oil company in Al-Sabaha, west of Sanaa”. The Saudi-led coalition had not yet confirmed the reported strike. Swiftly responding to the earlier coalition warning, the Houthis had issued a threat to target Riyadh’s international airport, a refinery, and an Aramco facility in Dammam if the strike went ahead. “The Yemeni Armed Forces urge all citizens to immediately evacuate and move away from targets that our forces will strike should the Saudi enemy target,” military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X, identifying the three targets. An attack at Riyadh’s airport on Saturday left 13 people dead and operations suspended, rocking the world’s top crude oil exporter and deepening the war in Yemen, where the kingdom backs the internationally recognised government. An AFP correspondent reported that many civilians in Sanaa, fearing shortages, rushed to queue in front of fuel stations after the coalition warning. The Yemen Petroleum Company sought to reassure the public, saying it had taken all necessary precautions in the event of an emergency to “meet people’s needs”. Petroleum stocks were “available in safe facilities and locations, and in sufficient quantities” to meet demand for long periods, it said. Saudi Arabia was still weathering fresh attacks on Tuesday, with the coalition saying its forces intercepted three drones north of the kingdom’s capital Riyadh. Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, most recently France, which told its citizens to avoid the airports in Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam on Tuesday. The Saudi coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis. Economic woes Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week, as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists. Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3 per cent, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Tehran’s chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz, vital for oil and gas trade, since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran. But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil. Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea — Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route. In Yemen, the renewed fighting was fuelling the risk of infectious disease outbreaks. Suspected cholera cases tripled there in three weeks, the World Health Organisation said on Tuesday, warning that the growing disease burden was straining hospitals already treating war casualties. Houthi warning Blasts were heard over the Saudi capital again late on Monday, with the Saudi coalition saying it intercepted a Houthi missile and the group announcing it had again targeted the airport. On Monday evening, Human Resources Minister Ahmad bin Sulaiman Al Rajhi remained defiant. “We’re not going out,” he told the crowd at the Riyadh Economic Forum. “We are safe. With God’s will. May God turn their plots back against them.” The Riyadh airport attack prompted US President Donald Trump to say he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis, after having reportedly rebuffed previous Saudi requests. The Houthis warned the US against intervention, with political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti telling AFP they would target American interests in the region. Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.

items.title: Appeal court panel hands off SERAP’s N101m defamation appeal
items.description: The Court of Appeal in Abuja on Tuesday returned the case files in two appeals arising from a N101 million defamation judgment in favour of two operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) to the Presiding Judge for reassignment. The appeals were filed by the Incorporated Trustees of the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) and by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Ogundare. The High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) awarded the damages in May. The panel had earlier heard the first appeal and reserved judgment. It later vacated that order, ruling that the two appeals, which emanated from one judgment, should be heard together for a composite judgment. The development was the second setback in the matter. Last week, proceedings in Ogundare’s appeal were halted midway. Before the panel vacated its order, a brief drama played out when SERAP’s lead counsel, Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, told the court that an application was pending for certain persons to be joined as amici curiae (friends of the court). Prof Olarewaju Fagbohun, SAN, a former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, rose to address the panel. He said he appeared for the Columbia Global Freedom of Expression Initiative of Columbia University and for the United Nations Special Rapporteurs on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association, and to freedom of opinion and expression. He said the application, filed on October 12 under Order 6 Rule 1 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021 and Section 6(6)(a) of the 1999 Constitution, sought leave to participate in the appeal. “We’re seeking the leave of this Hon court to participate in this appeal and assist the court with independent submissions,” he said. He added that the proposed brief would offer independent legal analysis and relevant comparative and international jurisprudence. The panel’s lead judge, Justice Danlami Senchi, was unimpressed. “Did the court invite you? Let’s be serious. This is the kind of image we create that is not good for us. We didn’t invite you. On behalf of whom?” he asked. He added: “I said earlier that we are not here to speak long grammar or waste the court’s time. We didn’t seek for any assistance.” Fagbohun replied: “We are not adversarial. We’re actually trying to assist this court.” Justice Senchi said every matter is decided on its merits and that an outsider could be heard only if its interests would be injured. “But you’re not a party in the lower court and in this court,” he said, asking the professor to withdraw the application “so that we can make progress.” Fagbohun withdrew the application and apologised to the court. The judge commended him: “Your juniors here will be happy for that.” Mojirayo Ogunlana, who appeared for the Southern African Litigation Centre, also withdrew her application to be admitted as amicus curiae. The panel then turned to Ogundare’s appeal, the same one that stalled last Friday. Midway into the hearing of an application for enlargement of time by the appellant’s counsel, Oluwatosin Adesoye, the court voiced displeasure with his presentation, saying he “should have sought the counsel of your seniors.” “Look at the way and manner you couched your prayers. We can’t grant this. You have to withdraw and refile it,” Justice Senchi said. “This is a court of record. You’re before the Court of Appeal.” The judge then announced: “We are sending this case file back for reassignment.” In its appeal, SERAP argues that the judgment was legally and procedurally flawed. Its Appellant’s Brief of Argument, filed by Oyetibo, raises 24 grounds challenging the finding of liability, the damages and the consequential orders. The group says the central question is whether the claimants proved by credible evidence that the publications referred to them. “The publications did not name the respondents, and the descriptions relied upon were general physical descriptions which did not, without more, identify the particular individuals who brought the action,” SERAP said. The publications followed SERAP’s call on President Bola Tinubu to investigate alleged corruption at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and reverse fuel price increases. SERAP had alleged that DSS officers entered its Abuja office without proper notice, describing two of them as “a tall, large, dark-skinned woman” and “a slim, dark-skinned man.” SERAP argues that neither publication identified the claimants by name, rank, designation, office or photograph. It adds that the claimants called no independent witness to show that an ordinary member of the public read the publications and understood them to refer to the two officers. “No independent witness was called to establish the alleged identification, while the social-media reactions relied upon by the respondents were not tendered in evidence,” the group said. SERAP also accuses the trial court of supplying the missing identification link by relying, among other things, on its own observation of the claimants’ physical appearance during proceedings. “The issue was whether the publications identified the respondents when they were published, not whether the respondents happened to fit the descriptions when they appeared before the Court,” it said. The group further describes the ₦100 million damages as excessive and unsupported by sufficient evidence. It says the trial court relied on claims that the publications affected the officers “mentally and psychologically” and had “gone viral,” without evidence of the extent of publication or of specific professional, financial or reputational injury. The post Appeal court panel hands off SERAP’s N101m defamation appeal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Court hands Adjetey Sowah, two others lifetime bans after Amputee Football legal dispute
items.description: A High Court judgment has handed Francis Adjetey Sowah and two others associated with the Ghana Amputee Football Federation (GAFF) lifetime bans following a decade-long legal dispute. The court rejected claims of the Ghana Amputee Football Federation (GAFF) in its dispute with the National Paralympic Committee of Ghana (NPC-Ghana) and handed the culprits a significant legal setback, while also referencing World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF) correspondence documenting lifetime bans involving three individuals associated with the organisation. The judgment, delivered on July 30, 2026, by Justice Jerome Noble-Nkrumah at the Commercial Division of the High Court in Accra, ruled against GAFF’s claims to exclusive responsibility for the administration and oversight of amputee football in Ghana. The court also granted relief to NPC Ghana on its counterclaim, permanently restraining GAFF and those acting through it from presenting the federation as the lawful body responsible for overseeing amputee football in the country. Court Records Lifetime Bans Against Three Individuals One of the most consequential passages in the judgment appears on page 21, where the court examined an email from WAFF dated September 25, 2019. According to the judgment, the correspondence referred to the banning of Francis Adjetey Sowah, Charles Narh and Benjamin Armah from amputee football for life, citing ethical breaches involving the three individuals. The judgment records the contents of the WAFF correspondence. This distinction is important: the lifetime bans are referenced in the evidence considered by the court, while the operative injunction specifically addresses GAFF’s claim to lawful oversight of amputee football in Ghana. Sowah’s Conduct Comes Under Judicial Scrutiny The court’s assessment of Sowah’s conduct was another significant aspect of the ruling. The judgment states that evidence showed Sowah was promoting GAFF’s affairs while serving as an officer of the Ghana Amputee Football Association, describing the activity as having been carried out “surreptitiously” before he was discovered and removed. The judge also examined correspondence bearing Sowah’s signature on the Association’s letterhead, including letters seeking equipment, logistics and sponsorship. The court contrasted those documents with Sowah’s subsequent use of GAFF letterhead in his capacity as the federation’s president, finding that the evidence seriously weakened GAFF’s claim to being the sole recognised authority responsible for the sport. These findings formed part of the court’s assessment of the federation’s claim to exclusive control over amputee football in Ghana. GAFF’s Incorporation History Raises Questions The court also considered evidence concerning GAFF’s stated objectives when it was incorporated in 2009. According to the judgment, a witness for the federation acknowledged that its original objectives did not include the organisation, administration and management of amputee football. Those objectives were added in 2014. The judge considered this admission alongside the evidence concerning Sowah’s roles within the organisations, further undermining GAFF’s argument that it was entitled to exclusive responsibility for the sport. The court ultimately found that GAFF had failed to establish its claims, while NPC Ghana succeeded on its counterclaim. Court Restrains GAFF From Claiming Lawful Oversight The judgment’s immediate institutional consequence is a permanent injunction restraining GAFF, including those acting through its servants, agents, assigns or privies, from holding itself out as the lawful oversight body for amputee football in Ghana. The court’s decision was based in part on the federation’s lack of recognition from the National Sports Authority, NPC Ghana and WAFF, as outlined in the judgment. Although GAFF argued that its history of official engagement supported its recognition and that amputee football should not fall under NPC Ghana, the court was not persuaded by its case. The judge acknowledged that the institutional placement of the sport could merit further consideration in the future. However, that observation did not alter the outcome of the proceedings. Other Names Mentioned, but No Additional Lifetime Bans Established John Kuuku Dsani and Philip Richter have also featured in public reporting surrounding the dispute. However, the judgment’s specific passage recording lifetime bans names only Francis Adjetey Sowah, Charles Narh and Benjamin Armah. It does not establish separate individual lifetime bans against all five men mentioned in the broader reporting. The ruling represents a major development in the dispute over the governance of amputee football in Ghana. By rejecting GAFF’s claims and granting NPC Ghana relief on its counterclaim, the High Court has placed a clear legal restriction on the federation’s ability to present itself as the country’s lawful amputee-football oversight body. The judgment also brings renewed attention to the WAFF correspondence documenting lifetime bans involving three individuals associated with the dispute. For Ghanaian amputee football, the decision marks a significant moment in the continuing debate over recognition, authority and the administration of the sport. The ruling also clears the air surrounding the leadership of the Black Challenge as they continue to prepare for the upcoming WAFF 2026 Amputee World Cup in Mexico in November.

items.title: Ogun hospital workers begin 3-day strike after patient’s relative stabs medical scientist
items.description: Healthcare workers at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Abeokuta, Ogun State, have begun a three-day warning strike following the alleged stabbing of a medical laboratory scientist, Lawal Toheeb Olasunkanmi, by a patient’s relative. Olasunkanmi was reportedly attacked on Sunday night while on duty at the hospital. A video shared on X showed the medical laboratory scientist bleeding from his nose as the alleged assailant threatened him. The incident prompted members of the hospital’s Joint Action Committee, comprising nurses, medical laboratory scientists and other non-academic staff, to commence the industrial action on Monday. In a notice issued on Monday, the committee condemned the attack and demanded measures to ensure the safety of healthcare workers within the facility. “On behalf of the leadership and entire members of our union, we write to express our profound displeasure, outrage, and deep concern over the unfortunate and unacceptable incident in which one of our colleagues (mr Lawal Toheeb Olasunkanmi), a Medical Laboratory Scientist, was stabbed by a patient’s relative last night within our Centre,” the notice read. The committee described the incident as an assault on the dignity, safety and welfare of healthcare professionals, insisting that violence against workers providing essential medical services should not be tolerated. It said hospitals should be safe environments for both patients and healthcare workers, adding that disagreements over medical services could not justify physical attacks. “No healthcare worker deserves to be threatened, assaulted, or stabbed in the course of providing care. Disagreement, frustration, or dissatisfaction with any service rendered in the hospital cannot justify violence under any circumstance,” the union said. The committee further described the attack as a collective concern for the hospital’s workforce, warning that workers could not remain silent while their safety was threatened. It called on the hospital management to formally report the incident to the appropriate law enforcement authorities and ensure that the alleged assailant was investigated and prosecuted in accordance with the law. The unions also warned against attempts to conceal or downplay the incident or resolve it in a manner that would undermine accountability. They demanded prompt and comprehensive medical treatment for Olasunkanmi, psychological support where necessary, and institutional assistance throughout his recovery. Meanwhile, the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to immediately arrest and prosecute the suspect allegedly involved in the attack. In a statement issued on Tuesday by Ado Bako, Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Salako described the incident as “barbaric and unacceptable”. “No grief, frustration or dissatisfaction with care can justify violence against a health worker performing his lawful duties,” the minister said. Salako also urged the striking healthcare workers to return to their duties in the interest of patients and the wider public. He called on the hospital management to ensure that the injured worker received appropriate medical attention and support, while strengthening security arrangements in line with Federal Government directives. The minister also extended his condolences to the family of the deceased patient and advised members of the public to channel complaints about hospital services through appropriate formal procedures. items.title: Ghana repatriates 120 Nigerians rescued from suspected cybercrime centres
items.description: The Minister of Communications, Samuel Nartey George, has announced that Ghana has returned 120 Nigerian nationals to their home country following an operation that uncovered suspected cybercrime activities and alleged human trafficking. The exercise, known as Operation Cyberhunt, brought together Ghanaian security agencies and international partners to tackle criminal networks operating in the country. Mr George said the individuals had been brought to Ghana and forced to work in cybercrime operations. He expressed gratitude to the Ghana Air Force and the Ministry of Defence for supporting their repatriation. The operation also yielded a substantial cache of electronic equipment, including 136 mobile phones, 130 laptops and internet connectivity devices. Four vehicles were seized, one of which was reportedly stolen from Canada. Investigators also recovered jewellery and 10 Nigerian passports during the operation. The minister disclosed that eight other individuals were being processed for prosecution but did not specify the offences they were expected to face. The Cyber Security Authority led the operation, working with local security and intelligence agencies and counterparts in the United Kingdom, Nigeria and the United States. Mr George said the exercise formed part of the government’s efforts to disrupt cybercrime networks and prevent the country from becoming a base for criminal activity. “Ghana under President John Dramani Mahama will remain an unfavourable destination for cyber criminals,” he said. The operation underscores the intersection of cybercrime and human trafficking, with authorities seeking to dismantle suspected criminal networks while addressing the alleged exploitation of people recruited into their activities. Investigations into the operation and the individuals involved are continuing. The minister has not publicly provided further details about the identities of those repatriated or the specific activities they were allegedly compelled to undertake.

items.title: Shanhui Zhang, Chercheure au Center for China & Globalization : « La Chine et les États-Unis décident d’organiser leur coexistence plutôt que de la subir »
items.description: Taïwan, guerre commerciale, Intelligence artificielle (Ia), etc. Entre la Chine et les États-Unis, les points de friction et de contradictions sont aussi nombreux. Avec la dernière visite du président chinois Xi Jinping, qui fait suite à celle de son homologue américain Donald Trump à Beijing, la rivalité-dualité entre ces deux puissances semble se normaliser. Chercheure au Center for China & Globalization et diplômée en gestion et commerce international de l’Université de la Sorbonne, en France, Shanhui Zhang analyse, dans cet entretien, les relations entre ces grands pays à l’aune de la compétition qu’ils se livrent. Entretien réalisé par Oumar NDIAYE Comment faut-il interpréter la visite de Xi Jinping aux États-Unis ? Véritable tournant dans les relations sino-américaines ou simple trêve dans une rivalité stratégique ? Ni l'un ni l'autre. Et c'est précisément ce qui fait la valeur de cette visite. Le mot juste est celui que les deux capitales ont choisi elles-mêmes : une relation constructive de stabilité stratégique, fondée sur le respect, l'équité et la réciprocité. Ce n'est pas la lune de miel de 1979, ce n'est pas non plus la guerre froide fantasmée par certains cercles à Washington. C'est une troisième voie, celle que la Chine défend depuis des années : deux grandes puissances qui se reconnaissent comme telles et qui décident d'organiser leur coexistence plutôt que de la subir. Regardons d'abord la méthode. En mai, lors de la visite de Trump à Beijing, les deux chefs d'État avaient fixé l'orientation suivante : privilégier la coopération, encadrer la concurrence, maîtriser les divergences et préserver la paix. Quatre mois plus tard, à Washington, les deux parties en ont précisé le contenu et la Chine en a donné la lecture suivante. Le respect, c'est celui de la souveraineté, de l'intégrité territoriale, du système social et de la voie de développement que chacun a choisie. L'équité, c'est refuser le jeu à somme nulle et l'avantage unilatéral. La réciprocité, c'est l'égalité souveraine entre deux pays, sans rapport de supériorité, sans intimidation, avec un traitement symétrique des préoccupations de chacun. Côté américain, la fiche de la Maison-Blanche parle d'une relation équitable et réciproque, un vocabulaire qui n'existait pas dans la bouche d'un président américain il y a deux ans, quand Washington ne parlait que de compétition et de garde-fous. Le véritable changement ne se lit pas dans les accords signés, mais dans les mots que les deux parties ont choisis pour se parler. Regardons ensuite les signes. Trump est allé accueillir le président chinois Xi Jinping en personne sur le tarmac de la base aérienne d'Andrews, une première depuis 1962. Deux visites d'État croisées en six mois, qualifiées par Beijing d'historiques, puis l'engagement mutuel de se soutenir pour l'Apec de Shenzhen et le G20 de Miami au dernier trimestre. Et au-delà des communiqués, les peuples : 100 000 jeunes Américains invités en Chine sur cinq ans, deux pandas pour Atlanta. Wang Yi, ministre des Affaires étrangères de la Chine, l'a résumé d'une formule ancienne : seuls les liens du cœur durent. La Chine ne demande pas aux États-Unis de l'aimer. Elle leur demande de la traiter d'égal à égal, et le message commence à passer. Les accords commerciaux annoncés peuvent-ils réellement contribuer à réduire les tensions économiques entre Washington et Pékin ? Oui, à condition de les lire pour ce qu'ils sont : un mécanisme. Chaque pays a désigné 30 milliards de dollars de biens pour un traitement tarifaire plus favorable. La Chine baisse ses droits sur les produits agricoles, les produits de soin, les dispositifs médicaux et le charbon américains. Les États-Unis baissent les leurs sur les jouets, l'électroménager, les articles pour bébés et les cadeaux de fêtes venus de Chine. Un groupe de travail agricole est créé sous le Conseil du commerce, avec une première réunion avant la fin de l'année. Ce qui compte, ce n'est pas le montant — modeste face à environ 575 milliards d'échanges annuels— mais la méthode. Depuis Kuala Lumpur, la relation fonctionne par consultations régulières et résultats cumulatifs, exactement ce que la Chine réclamait quand elle refusait les ultimatums de 2025. Les tarifs unilatéraux n'ont produit ni relocalisation massive ni effondrement chinois. Les États-Unis reviennent donc à la table, avec le vocabulaire de la réduction mutuelle. Regardez la liste américaine : des biens du quotidien dont le prix a grimpé avec la guerre commerciale. Washington reconnaît, sans le dire, que le consommateur américain payait la facture. La Chine, elle, obtient la prévisibilité. On dira que la trêve n'est prolongée que de deux mois. Deux mois renouvelables, avec deux sommets en vue où les deux Présidents ont dit vouloir se retrouver. C'est une chaîne de rendez-vous, pas une échéance couperet. La tension ne disparaît pas ; elle devient gérable. La question de Taïwan reste l’un des principaux points de tension. Cette visite de Xi Jinping permet-elle d’envisager une meilleure gestion du risque de confrontation ? Taïwan est une ligne rouge pour la Chine et cette visite l'a rappelé sans ambiguïté. Xi Jinping a été très clair : la position chinoise sur l'unité nationale et l'intégrité territoriale ne souffre d’aucune interprétation. Il a demandé aux États-Unis de maintenir leur opposition à l'indépendance de Taïwan et de traiter la question avec prudence parce que c'est sur ce socle que se construit la coopération stratégique. Par ailleurs, la Chine propose un cadre pour que les désaccords ne se règlent pas par accident : un mémorandum sur la communication et la prévention des crises, un dialogue militaire régulier. Ce qu'il faut comprendre, c'est d'où vient la menace. Pour la Chine, elle est double. D’abord, les activités séparatistes des forces indépendantistes d'abord, ensuite l'ingérence extérieure. Et les deux se nourrissent l'une l'autre. Chaque livraison d'armes, chaque « transit » d'un dirigeant de Taïwan aux États-Unis, chaque loi du Congrès envoie un signal aux séparatistes et fait monter la température. La gestion du risque commence par-là : ne pas encourager ceux qui veulent changer le statu quo. Face à la montée de la rivalité technologique, notamment dans l’Intelligence artificielle (IA), les États-Unis et la Chine peuvent-ils à la fois coopérer et rester des concurrents stratégiques ? Non seulement c'est possible, mais c'est la seule option rationnelle. Le développement sûr et ordonné de l’Intelligence artificielle engage l'avenir de l'humanité et il ne se fera pas sans la Chine et les États-Unis. Les deux Présidents ont acté un dialogue bilatéral sur l'Ia, dès novembre, pour échanger sur les risques et les bénéfices et prévenir ensemble les usages malveillants. Regardez la table du dîner d'État : Tim Cook, Jensen Huang, Sam Altman, Elon Musk. Tous savent que l'Ia sans la Chine est une Ia sans la moitié des ingénieurs, des données et des chaînes d'approvisionnement de la planète. Xi Jinping a fixé le cadre : les deux pays ont la capacité et la responsabilité de garder l'Ia sous contrôle humain et au service des peuples, et ils doivent faire valoir leurs atouts respectifs plutôt que de se barricader l'un contre l'autre. Sur la rivalité, soyons lucides. Les contrôles sur les puces restent, la course aux modèles continue. Mais, la concurrence n'a jamais empêché la coopération sur les risques. Américains et Soviétiques négociaient des traités nucléaires en pleine guerre froide. La vraie question n'est pas de savoir dans quelle mesure les deux puissances peuvent coopérer. C'est de savoir si l'Ia sera un bien public mondial ou le privilège de deux pays. Sur ce point, la position chinoise est connue : l'Ia doit profiter à tous et le Sud global ne doit pas revivre la fracture numérique qu'il a déjà subie.

items.title: NPP rejects Emelia Agbenyo’s appointment as Deputy EC Chair, demands withdrawal
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has rejected the appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC), calling on President John Mahama to withdraw the appointment over concerns about her previous political activities. In a statement issued by the National Communications Director, Miracles Aboagye, on Tuesday, October 13, the party questioned Ms Agbenyo’s ability to demonstrate political neutrality, citing her role as a governance sector spokesperson during the National Democratic Congress (NDC)’s preparation of its 2024 manifesto and her alleged participation in the party’s campaign activities. The NPP argued that her appointment to the leadership of the institution responsible for overseeing Ghana’s elections could undermine public confidence in the Electoral Commission, particularly ahead of the 2028 general elections. The party said Ms Agbenyo had appeared at NDC campaign rallies and worn party-branded T-shirts while advocating for the party, arguing that such activities raised concerns about the perception of impartiality expected of an electoral commissioner. The NPP also cited President Mahama’s criticism in March 2023 of appointments he described as involving political activists at the Electoral Commission. According to the party, the President had called for an amendment to Article 43(2) of the 1992 Constitution to require parliamentary approval for such appointments. It accused the President of acting contrary to the position he had previously expressed and said the issue required public scrutiny. “The consequences are serious,” the party said, warning that a loss of public confidence in the EC could lead to suspicion surrounding voter registration, boundary decisions and the declaration of election results. The NPP called on President Mahama to withdraw Ms Agbenyo’s appointment and urged the Council of State to explain the advice it gave on the nomination. It further appealed to the government to use the ongoing constitutional review process to reform the appointment of Electoral Commission members, in line with the proposal the President reportedly made in 2023. The party maintained that it would use lawful means to protect the integrity of Ghana’s electoral system and called on civil society organisations, religious bodies, the media and other citizens to support its demand. Read also: Mahama swears in Emelia Afi Agbenyo, Joseph Kwaku Asamoah as EC Deputy Commissioners Ms Agbenyo was sworn into office on October 12, 2026, alongside Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah, to fill vacancies created by the departure of former Deputy Chairpersons Dr Bossman Eric Asare and Samuel Tettey. President Mahama urged the two appointees to discharge their constitutional responsibilities independently and impartially, without favouring any political party or candidate.

items.title: Le ministre de la Justice suspend un garde pénitentiaire pour avoir transporté des civils dans un véhicule d’extraction de détenus
items.description: Le ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme a annoncé, ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, la suspension conservatoire du brigadier Mamady Oularé, un garde pénitentiaire accusé d’avoir transporté des passagers civils à bord d’un véhicule destiné à l’extraction de détenus. Selon le communiqué du département, un incident « traduisant un manquement grave aux procédures administratives et d’escorte des détenus » a été constaté le dimanche 11 octobre 2026. Les faits se sont produits lors d’une mission officielle de transfert de prévenus de la Maison d’arrêt et de correction de Coyah vers la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), en prélude à une audience correctionnelle prévue le lundi 12 octobre. Au cours de cette mission, le brigadier Mamady Oularé « a dévié sa mission principale en utilisant le véhicule d’extraction pour transporter des passagers civils sur le trajet à l’aller », indique le ministère. Face à ce comportement, le département estime que « ce comportement individuel de l’agent est en totale contradiction avec le code de déontologie et les règles strictes qui régissent le corps du personnel pénitentiaire ». Le ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme dit condamner fermement les faits, dénonçant « cet acte irresponsable qui ternit l’image de l’institution ». Trois mesures ont été annoncées à la suite de cet incident : « la suspension conservatoire de l’agent concerné », « l’ouverture d’une enquête disciplinaire sans préjudice de poursuites pénales » et « le renforcement des contrôles des convois pénitentiaires pour éviter toute récidive ». À travers ces mesures, le département entend prévenir de nouveaux manquements et renforcer le respect des règles encadrant le transport des détenus. Le ministère réaffirme enfin « son engagement constant à garantir la sécurité des citoyens et à faire respecter la loi avec rigueur et intégrité ». Ousmane CAMARA L’article Le ministre de la Justice suspend un garde pénitentiaire pour avoir transporté des civils dans un véhicule d’extraction de détenus est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Forex inflow rises 23% to $35 billion
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Nigeria’s net foreign exchange (forex) inflow grew by 23.2 percent year-on-year, YoY to $35.77 billion in the first half of 2026 (H1’26) from $29.77 in the corresponding period of 2025. Vanguard analysis of data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Quarterly Statistical Bulletin and Data for the review period showed that aggregate forex inflow rose by 12.7 per cent to $63.82 billion in H1’26 from $56.62 billion in H1’25. However, forex outflow declined by 25.5 per cent to $19.98 billion from $26.85 billion recorded in H1’25. According to the report, forex inflow through the CBN fell slightly by 0.27 per cent to $18.28 billion from $18.33 billion in H1’25, while inflow through autonomous sources increased by 18.7 per cent to $45.5 billion in H1’26 from $38.3 billion in H1’25. But forex outflow through the bank dropped by 40.4 per cent to $12.2 billion from $20.47 billion in H1’25. However, outflow through autonomous sources increased by 21.8 per cent to $7.8 billion from $6.4 billion in H1’25. Consequently, autonomous sources recorded a net forex inflow of $37.7 billion in H1’26 compared with $31.89 billion in H1’25. The Bank on its part recorded a net forex inflow of $6.12 billion in H1’26, higher than the -$2.13 billion recorded in H1’25.
