items.title: EOCO grants Suame MP John Darko enquiry bail in GH¢27m SIC investigation
items.description: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has granted Suame Member of Parliament John Darko enquiry bail after he reported to investigators to assist with an ongoing investigation into an alleged criminal conspiracy involving SIC Savings and Loans Company Limited. In a news release dated October 13, 2026, EOCO said Mr Darko honoured its invitation and reported to the Office at exactly 12 noon to provide information relevant to the investigation. The EOCO statement comes days after John Darko disclosed on Saturday, October 3, 2026, that he had been told he was also involved in the investigation into Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, saying he would cooperate if invited. “I have been told that I’m also involved. I don’t know. And so I will wait until I get an invitation from them. Then I can go and tell whatever I know,” he said. READ ALSO: ‘I’ve been told I’m also involved’ – John Darko says he’ll cooperate with EOCO if invited over Baffour Awuah case Darko, who is also Legal Counsel to the Minority Caucus, had previously condemned EOCO’s attempt to arrest Baffour Awuah at the Accra High Court on September 23, 2026, describing the incident as unacceptable and warning that no state institution should operate above the Constitution. The investigation concerns alleged unauthorised financial transactions at SIC Life Savings and Loans Company Limited. Baffour Awuah, who is the Senior Partner of Sarkodie Baffour Awuah & Partners, was engaged by SIC Life in May 2020 to recover a debt from Equity Savings and Loans Limited. In July 2024, SIC Life, Equity, and Eco Swiss Investment Limited executed Terms of Settlement under which SIC Life agreed to accept GH¢5,000,000.00 in full and final settlement of a revised judgment debt of GH¢14,850,776.14. The State alleges the MP was instrumental in arranging the transaction and later transferred GH¢1,000,000.00 to the then Managing Director of SIC Life. Baffour Awuah has been charged with conspiracy to commit a crime (intentional dissipation of public funds), intentionally causing financial loss to a public body, and money laundering. He is expected to be arraigned before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division. The Office described the MP as cooperative throughout the process. “The Honourable Member was respectful, cooperative and fully responsive throughout the investigative process,” EOCO said. It added that the decision to grant him enquiry bail was based on the circumstances of the case, the applicable law and his level of cooperation with investigators. EOCO said the investigation concerns an alleged criminal conspiracy that has resulted in a revised estimated financial loss of approximately GH¢27 million to SIC Savings and Loans Company Limited. The Office did not provide further details about the specific allegations against Mr Darko in the release. EOCO stressed that investigations were ongoing and that no conclusion had been reached regarding the culpability of any person connected to the matter. The grant of enquiry bail does not, in itself, establish wrongdoing by the MP. EOCO also disclosed that the former Managing Director of SIC Life Savings and Loans, Amma Frimpomaa Dwumah, has honoured its invitation and is cooperating with investigators. EOCO said investigations remain active and no conclusion has been reached regarding the culpability of any person connected to the matter. Further updates are expected as the investigation progresses.

items.title: Pension: Why we ‘re targeting informal sector- Pencom D-G
items.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The National Pension Commission is targeting Nigeria’s informal sector to secure the participation of the nation’s largest group of workers in the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). The Director-General of Pencom, Ms. Omolola Oloworaran, who spoke at the 2026 National Pension Commission Media Conference in Abuja, yesterday, said that with the informal sector accounting for about 92 percent of the nation’s workforce, it must be included in the pension reform for it to be considered successful. She spoke on the theme, “From Reform To Reality, Renewed Hope, Pension Security for Nigerians”. The D-G said that her team was giving the Personal Pension Plan for the informal sector a very strong push to enable them benefit from the various programmes targeting pensioners in the country. According to her, PenCom has engaged accredited pension agents targeting workers in the informal sector and that the commission was in the process on accrediting more agents for the same purpose. She said that the agents were taking the Personal Pension Plan to markets, motor parks, farms and workshops to enroll traders, artisans, farmers and transport workers. Tinubu most Pro-Pensioners President Ms. Oloworaran said President Bola Tinubu was laying the foundation for a sustainable social security in the country through enhanced welfare for retirees with increased pensions and the free health to be launched at the end of this month. The Pencom boss described President Tinubu as, “the most pro-retiree president, going by the achievements recorded so far in the pension industry. “From the very beginning of pensions in the country to all the reforms that have happened, he is the most pro-worker, most pro-retiree President we have seen in the history of Nigeria,” she said. Ms. Oloworaran said that the administration had settled N758 billion inherited pension obligations (with nearly one million pensioners benefiting from the payment), introduced new benefits, accelerated payment of retirement benefits and improved pension security for workers and retirees. She said that for the first time in 21 years, pensions of 2,116 retirees of the defunct Nigerian Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) were reviewed, citing an example of a particular pensioner on N18, 000 monthly, now receiving N206,000. “Twenty-one years of waiting was answered in a single decision,” she said. According to her, retirement benefits that previously took up to 21 months to approve are now approved within 48 hours for federal government workers. The D-G said that two additional initiatives would be unveiled during the National Pension Week scheduled for October 26 to October 30. She said that one of them was “PenCare,” a retiree healthcare programme that would provide eligible low-income retirees with essential healthcare at no cost during its pilot phase. The pilot stage would cover 30,000 retirees. The post Pension: Why we ‘re targeting informal sector- Pencom D-G appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NPP cannot question EC appointment after appointing own people to Commission – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has defended the appointment of Emelia Affi Agbenyo to the Electoral Commission (EC), accusing the New Patriotic Party (NPP) of double standards in its criticism of the decision. The NPP has raised concerns about the appointment, arguing that Ms Agbenyo’s previous association with the National Democratic Congress (NDC), including her role as a spokesperson on the party’s manifesto committee, could raise questions about her impartiality as the Deputy Chairperson of the commission. But speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Kwakye Ofosu argued that the NPP was not in a position to question the appointment, given what he described as the party’s own record of appointing people with known political affiliations to the Commission. “At the last count, there were at least four known NPP deputies on the Electoral Commission,” he said. He cited the EC’s chairperson and other officials, including the recently resigned Deputy Chairperson, Dr Bossman Asare, and Dr Appiahene, whom he described as having publicly acknowledged their NPP affiliations. He also mentioned Madam Salima Tijani, whom he identified as another person associated with the NPP who had been appointed to the Commission. “How can a party that made these appointments to the Electoral Commission turn around and purport to be upset or angry over the appointment of an individual?” he asked. Mr Kwakye Ofosu acknowledged that Ms Agbenyo had worked with the NDC in the past but said he believed she had the qualities needed to perform her new role professionally. “It is true that Affi Agbenyo has worked in some capacities for the NDC, but I know her as a person, that she has the right temperament. She has the academic and professional standing. She has the presence of mind to operate professionally in the role that has been assigned to her,” he said. He conceded that some people might have concerns about whether her political association could affect perceptions of fairness and balance at the Commission. However, he maintained that the NPP’s own appointments to the EC weakened its criticism of the government’s decision.

items.title: 2027: Olawepo-Hashim slams opposition figures in APC campaign council as ‘indiscipline, rascality’
items.description: The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has described the inclusion of opposition figures in the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign council as “indiscipline and rascality”. Olawepo-Hashim made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he reacted to the inclusion of opposition figures like Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo in the APC campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections. Asked whether the move reflected political maturity or political survival, the Accord Party candidate dismissed both interpretations, describing it instead as a lack of discipline. “No, this is simply indiscipline and rascality,” he said. Olawepo-Hashim also argued that Adeleke’s participation in the APC campaign council would not automatically translate into support for President Bola Tinubu among voters in Osun State. He said the governor’s electoral victory did not give him the power to determine how the people of the state would vote in the presidential election. “Governor Adeleke, the fact that he won his election cannot compel the people of Osun State to vote for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. To support his argument, Olawepo-Hashim recalled the 2011 general election, when he said voters in Osun State did not follow the political direction of then Lagos State Governor, Bola Tinubu, after the latter allegedly backed the Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate, Goodluck Jonathan, instead of the Action Congress of Nigeria’s presidential candidate, Nuhu Ribadu. He said Osun voters supported Ribadu despite the reported political arrangement, arguing that the state’s electorate had a history of making independent political choices. “Osun people are incredibly honourable people, what we call Omoluabi in the Yoruba parlance; they are ideological; they have great history, they are not conquered people, they do what they believe,” he said. The Accord Party candidate maintained that Adeleke’s current political alignment would not prevent his party from seeking votes in Osun State during the presidential election. “I still believe that regardless of what Governor Adeleke is doing, Osun people are still going to vote for Accord Party at the presidential election,” he said. items.title: BoG deepens public trust with regional stakeholder forum in Techiman
items.description: As part of its strategic commitment to inclusive central banking and nationwide financial literacy, the Bank of Ghana (BoG) has held a high-level Regional Stakeholder Engagement Forum at the Jemima Grace Hotel, Techiman. The meeting took place on Monday, 12 October 2026, on the theme: Strengthening Stakeholder Relations Through Dialogue and Engagement. The forum forms part of the Bank’s 16-regional outreach programme aimed at demystifying the mandate of the central bank, deepening public confidence in the financial system, and creating direct feedback channels between the regulator and the public. The engagement brought together a broad spectrum of stakeholders in the Bono East Region, including traditional leaders, religious leaders, market queens and trader associations, SMEs, representatives of rural and community banks, microfinance institutions, security agencies, and media practitioners. A total of 150 participants attended the programme. The delegation for the forum was led by Bernard Otabil, Director of Communications, together with Victor Akakpo, Head of Regional Branch Coordinating Office, and Abdulai Lawal Abubakar, Regional Director, Sunyani, who has oversight responsibility for the Bono East Region. Technical presentations were delivered by seasoned experts from key departments of the Bank: Banking Supervision Department (BSD), Other Financial Institutions Supervision Department (OFISD), Financial Stability Department (FSD), and Currency Management Department (CMD) “The Cedi Is Trust” – Director of Communications In his opening remarks, Mr Otabil stressed that central banking cannot thrive in isolation, noting that stakeholder trust is the bedrock of monetary policy effectiveness. “The Cedi is not just paper. It is trust. It is a social contract between the Bank of Ghana and every Ghanaian. We can formulate the best monetary policy, but if the trader in the Techiman market, arguably one of the largest open markets in West Africa, does not understand or trust it, we have failed. That is why we are here, not to lecture, but to listen, to dialogue, and to partner for financial stability,” he stated. He added that BoG has deliberately shifted to a people-centred model where public voices shape policy response, especially in fighting unlicensed financial schemes, currency abuse, and misinformation. Participants were taken through five critical thematic areas: 1. The Role and Mandate of the Bank of Ghana: Clarifying BoG’s core functions of price stability, financial stability, and currency management. 2. Microfinance Sector Reforms: Explaining the rationale behind the Microfinance sector reforms and implications for the industry. 3. Responsible Borrowing and Consumer Protection: Educating the public on their rights, loan disclosure requirements, and the need to avoid over-indebtedness. 4. Currency Education – FEEL, LOOK, TILT: A practical demonstration on how to identify genuine Ghana Cedi banknotes, detect counterfeits, and properly handle notes. 5. Dud Cheques – Causes, Implications and Prevention: Highlighting the legal and financial consequences of issuing dud cheques and measures to curb the practice. Stakeholder Feedback In an open forum, participants commended the Bank for bringing the engagement to their doorstep. They raised pertinent concerns including access to affordable credit for SMEs and farmers, the persistence of high lending rates despite falling inflation, the activities of unregulated lenders and “black market” forex operators, and the need for sustained education on the security features of the new Heritage Series Banknotes. Officials of the Bank provided detailed responses and assured participants that their concerns would be escalated to Management for policy consideration. Mr Otabil reiterated the Bank’s commitment to sustaining open dialogue across all 16 regions as a tool for promoting financial inclusion, financial literacy, and resilience of the financial system. He urged the public to be vigilant and report suspected unlicensed financial institutions, counterfeit currency, and financial fraud cases to the Bank or law enforcement agencies. The forum ended with a renewed call for partnership between the Bank of Ghana and regional stakeholders to protect the value of the Cedi and safeguard the stability of Ghana’s financial system.

items.title: 5 killed, several injured as Peshawar-bound train derails in Punjab's Multan district
items.description: LAHORE: Five people were killed and several others were injured when the Peshawar-bound Rehman Baba Express derailed near Sher Shah Railway Station in Multan district on Tuesday, officials said. Pakistan Railways (PR) Chief Executive Officer Muhammad Hafeezullah confirmed the death toll to Dawn , adding that more than 40 had been injured. According to an initial investigation report by the PR, the derailment was likely caused by a fault in a passenger coach. Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi has appointed the federal government inspector of railways (FGIR) as the inquiry officer. “We have appointed the FGIR to probe the incident,” Abbasi told Dawn . Passengers sit with their belongings next to derailed coaches of the passenger train Rehman Baba Express on the outskirts of Multan on October 13, 2026. — AFP Speaking to Dawn , train driver Rizwan Abbas said the train was travelling at 100 kilometres per hour. “The signal was clear, and as I was passing through the Sher Shah station area, I suddenly felt a push,” he said. He said he applied the brakes and managed to bring the train to a stop. “When I got out of the locomotive and looked back, I saw that the passenger coaches had derailed and were lying off the tracks. It was horrible,” he said. Abbas maintained that the train was in working order. In an earlier statement, the railways minister expressed grief over the loss of life, saying he shared the sorrow of the bereaved families, according to an official statement. He directed the authorities to ensure the provision of the best possible medical facilities to the injured passengers and said compensation would be paid to the deceased and injured in accordance with the Pakistan Railways insurance policy, as per the statement. Meanwhile, a replacement train for the Rehman Baba Express, carrying more than 500 passengers, departed from Sher Shah Railway Station, according to a statement. Buses were also arranged in coordination with the Multan district administration for passengers wishing to continue their journeys by road. The statement added that all field formations of the Commercial Department were on high alert to facilitate passengers. Multan Commissioner Amir Karim Khan also met the affected passengers and their families and assured them of all possible assistance. Rescue workers search for the victims following the derailment of passenger train Rehman Baba Express on the outskirts of Multan on October 13, 2026. — AFP For its part, the PR set up round-the-clock information and help desks at all major stations to guide and assist passengers following the accident. Divisional commercial officers (DCOs) were also directed to arrange alternative travel options and ensure ticket refunds wherever necessary. Ministry working to resolve issues Speaking to the media later, the railways minister acknowledged that it was his responsibility to ensure safe journeys for passengers. “Before this, no one even tried to focus on the mechanical condition of trains,” he said. He described freight wagons as “dummies” because, he said, they did not have brakes. Abbasi added that his ministry was working to address problems with locomotives, coaches and wagons, setting Dec 31 as the deadline for the work to be completed. “All of this work will be completed by Dec 31,” Abbasi said. Asked whether he would resign, the minister said: “Have some patience. We need to investigate the incident first, and those responsible will be held accountable. In fact, I was just on a call with the prime minister. We are trying to prevent such incidents and making efforts to that end. Giving up and running away is not in our nature.” Abbasi expressed sorrow over the loss of lives, saying there could be no substitute for those who had died and that the incident should not have happened. President, PM express condolences President Asif Ali Zardari, in a statement on X, expressed concern over the incident, extending “heartfelt condolences and sympathy” to the bereaved families. He also expressed best wishes for the injured passengers’ early recovery. “The President directs relevant authorities to ensure assistance to the affected passengers and provision of all possible facilities. Transparent investigations should be conducted to determine the causes of the accident,” Zardari said. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over the deaths caused by the derailment. The premier took notice of the incident and instructed the relevant authorities to expedite rescue and relief operations, according to state-run Associated Press of Pakistan . He also called for providing immediate and the best possible medical facilities to the injured. “PM Shehbaz prayed for peace for the departed souls and strength for the bereaved families to bear the loss, besides sympathising with the affected families,” APP reported. Lack of maintenance There have been a series of train derailment incidents over the past year, raising concerns over possible negligence and deep-rooted issues of Pakistan Railways (PR) over maintenance of trains and tracks across the country. On October 1, two passenger trains, Shalimar Express and Pakistan Express, narrowly escaped major accidents after derailing, while a third minor accident also occurred on Jaffar Express on the track near Gujar Khan. At the time, PR Chief Executive Officer Hafeezullah said the accidents happened due to a lack of maintenance in the last five years, while claiming that a series of maintenance measures had been undertaken. In August, the Yousafwala coal train derailed near Firoza Railway Station (between Khanpur and Liaqatpur) after it ran into the sand hump on the loopline, apparently due to weak brakes or the driver not applying the brakes in time. The same day, a passenger train (Rawal Express) derailed near Kala Gujran in Jhelum district on the Main Line-1 (Lahore-Rawalpindi track), disrupting railway operations. On Aug 4, the Havailian-bound Hazara Express also met with an accident when its driver reportedly overshot and hit the sand hump, causing loss of rolling stock and other infrastructure. Similarly, Aug 5 saw another derailment as the Bulleh Shah Passenger train derailed. On July 28, the Lahore-bound Tezgam derailed between Hyderabad-Kotri sections while on the same day, Thal Express’s engine broke down near Muzaffargarh. On July 5, the Karachi-bound Shalimar Express had derailed near Khanewal. A Bulleh Shah passenger coach derailed in Lahore on July 20, while July 22 saw another major derailment when Hazara Express’ four passenger coaches derailed near the Karachi Cantt Railway station.

items.title: PTI protest in KP's Bara turns violent as demonstrators clash with police
items.description: KHYBER: A protest demonstration by the PTI workers in Khyber’s Bara tehsil turned violent on Tuesday as protesters clashed with police and government buildings were set ablaze. There were reports of police firing live rounds and tear gas and protesters manhandling law enforcers. Dawn was able to confirm injuries to at least five protesters, based on accounts by eyewitnesses, who asked not to be named, while police said 50 people had been arrested. However, a doctor at Hayatabad Medical Complex, one of the city’s three major hospitals, told Dawn that more than a dozen injured, including four policemen, had been brought to the facility. The protest was held against the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkwa — a move that has rendered PTI’s Sohail Afridi non-functional as the province’s chief minister — and emergency in 12 of its districts, including Khyber. Scores of PTI workers assembled at the Khyber Chowk in Bara Bazaar in the afternoon for the protest, following which police reached the site. There were reports of police initially resorting to baton-charge and tear gas shelling to disperse protesters. Eyewitnesses told Dawn that police managed to disperse some protesters but later local MPA Abdul Ghani Afridi also reached the site with more PTI supporters. The protesters forced police to retreat, with some of the law enforcers taking shelter in nearby shops and commercial buildings, according to eyewitnesses. Reports received from the area said protesters manhandled police and dragged them out of shops, following which law enforcers fired tear gas shells and live rounds in the air. There were also reports of the nearby National Database and Registration Authority’s office and a portion of the Rescue 1122 building being torched. Police eventually dispersed the protesters from Khyber Chowk but all roads leading to Bara Bazaar were closed even as the demonstration ended. Meanwhile, leaders of the Bara Siyasi Ittehad urged both PTI workers and police to avoid violent confrontation. Arrests Capital City Police Peshawar said in a statement that 50 “miscreant elements” in Bara who “attempted to spread unrest” had been arrested. Separately, the newly appointed adviser on information and broadcasting in KP, Samar Haroon Bilour, said, “Forty-two PTI-affiliated miscreants associated with vandalism and unrest have been arrested, of whom 25 are illegal Afghans.” She accused the protesters of damaging public and government property. The adviser alleged that some individuals, reportedly led by PTI leaders, attempted to create unrest at Bara Chowk. She added that police made arrests over the incident and brought the situation under control. Dawn could not independently verify the number of arrests, the extent of the damage and the nationality and immigration status of those detained.

items.title: ‘We have turned the tide’ – Ato Forson says Ghana is ready to take off
items.description: Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana has turned the tide from economic crisis and laid the foundation for sustained progress, but has cautioned that further gains will depend on protecting macroeconomic stability. According to him, the country was moving in the right direction, with the foundation now in place to support economic take-off. “Today we have turned the tide. We are moving the right direction. And I can assure you that based on the foundation that we have laid, this country is ready to take off,” Dr. Forson said. The Finance Minister, however, stressed that the turnaround was not a reason to abandon caution. He said the stability underpinning the recovery must remain central to the country’s next steps. “And we will take off cautiously. Bear in mind that all the gains we have made is dependent on us maintaining the macroeconomic stability,” he cautioned. Dr. Forson said building on the progress achieved must go hand in hand with preserving its foundations. “And so, the gains that we will build on, we should not forget the foundation that we have laid,” he added. He also reminded those entrusted with the country’s leadership that their mandate was to respond to a national crisis and work to the satisfaction of Ghanaians. “We were elected to come and save a country in crisis. Don’t forget that. President Mahama and his members of parliament were elected to save this country because Ghana was in a crisis. Let us not forget that,” he said. The Finance Minister emphasised that delivering on that mandate remained a shared responsibility, even as the country’s circumstances improved. “Together, we have a responsibility. A responsibility to work to the satisfaction of the people of Ghana,” he said.

items.description: The Ghana Police Service has arrested a 30-year-old farmer captured in a viral video assaulting his wife, Diana Mensah, 25, at Agona Nkwanta in the Western Region. In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 13, the suspect, identified as Emmanuel Kwofie, was arrested on Monday, October 12, 2026, at about 7:00 p.m. in Agona Nkwanta. According to the Western Regional Police Command, preliminary investigations indicate that the suspect and the victim are married and live together at Domeabra in the Agona Nkwanta Municipality. The victim deals in second-hand clothing. Police said the incident occurred on Thursday, October 8, after the suspect allegedly accused his wife of having an extramarital affair and subjected her to severe beating, as captured in the circulating video. The victim was rescued by a Good Samaritan and taken to the Agona Nkwanta Polyclinic, where she received treatment and was discharged. The suspect is currently in police custody and is expected to be put before court, the police said in a press release dated October 13, 2026. KATH Mother and Baby Unit construction stalled for 14 months over unpaid contractor arrears
items.description: The 509-bed Mother and Baby Unit designed to save the lives of mothers and babies is gathering dust at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), as contractors have yet again suspended construction for 14 months over unpaid arrears. Despite millions of dollars invested, the facility remains incomplete, with some procured materials now deteriorating and warranties expiring. Parliamentary Committee on Health is raising concerns over the prolonged delay, warning against the waste of taxpayers’ money as expectant mothers wait for a facility intended to transform maternal and child healthcare in the Ashanti Region and beyond. Expectant mothers in the Ashanti Region and beyond were anticipating a sigh of relief when contractors commenced construction of the mother and baby unit at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital. The building was expected to have been completed within three (3) years of its initiation in 2019 after demolition of the original 44-year-old block. However, construction works have suffered intermittent setbacks, with the project now exceeding its intended timelines. Parliament Select Committee on Health inspected the facility as part of its working visit to the region’s largest referral hospital. The abandoned structure is now approximately 70 per cent complete but remains suspended for about 14 months over non-payment of Interim Payment Certificates to the contractor. Project Consultant Emmanuel Fobi Asabre noted that the project had experienced two major suspensions, with the first lasting approximately 18 months, following which work resumed steadily before the new suspension. “The first suspension came during the domestic debt exchange programme (DDEP). We worked for another 12 months when we resumed work after the first suspension. Now, we have suspended again over the non-payment of IPCs to the contractor,” he noted. The hospital project was initially estimated at a budgetary allocation of $138.5 million, but the prolonged suspensions had resulted in additional costs. The physical construction is currently 56 per cent complete, with procurements standing at 75 per cent while demolition of the entire old block has been completed. The suspension has since affected the state of some procured materials and installations for the facility, with others losing their insurance warranties. “Some materials have already expired. Although we can apply for revalidation for others that have expired, the new timeline for resumption is preventing us from engaging the manufacturers for another validation. The ones that have been damaged have been removed out of site,” he said. Member of Parliament for Obuasi East, who is Deputy Ranking Member on the Committee, Dr. Patrick Boakye Yiadom, expressed disappointment at the prolonged delay in completing the maternity and children’s facility. Describing the state of the project as a “sad spectacle”, Dr. Boakye Yiadom stressed that a facility intended to provide healthcare for mothers and children must not remain incomplete for such an extended period. “This is a sad spectacle. A hospital that is supposed to provide healthcare for mothers and children. For good 50 years, we’ve not seen the hospital. We must make good use of the taxpayers’ money. I don’t see why this project is standing aloof at this time,” he noted. Chairman of the Committee, Dr. Mark Kurt Nawaane, said the construction difficulties confronting the project highlighted a broader challenge affecting public infrastructure development across the country. “The principle is clear: we must not continue to initiate projects without ensuring that adequate resources are available to complete them. They come and inspect as usual. If you raise your certificates, we will look for the money and pay. We are raising the money locally to finance the project,” he said. He continued: “The contractors don’t give up. It’s just a matter of sitting down and having common denominator”.

items.title: Moov Africa-ONATEL: les valeurs républicaines et patriotiques du Faso réaffirmées autour du drapeau national
items.description: La société de téléphonie Moov Africa-ONATEL a réaffirmé son engagement à promouvoir les valeurs républicaines et patriotiques du Burkina Faso, lors d’une cérémonie solennelle de montée des couleurs nationales, ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, au siège de l'entreprise à Ouagadougou. Cette activité se tient dans le cadre des Journées d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC), troisième édition, qui est célébrée sous le thème: « Produisons burkinabè, consommons burkinabè ». La direction générale de Moov Africa-ONATEL et ses six directions régionales au Burkina Faso, ont organisé, ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, des cérémonies officielles de montée des Couleurs nationales, dans le cadre des troisièmes Journées d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC) qui se déroulent du 2 au 16 octobre. A Ouagadougou, la cérémonie s’est déroulée au siège de la société, sis au Centre-ville. Bien plus qu’un simple rituel protocolaire, cette montée des Couleurs nationales a été un moment sacré de communion patriotique qui a rassemblé les travailleurs autour du drapeau. Une vue des responsables de Moov Africa-ONATEL À l'occasion de ces JEPPC, placée sous le thème national: « Produisons burkinabè, consommons burkinabè », les employés de la société arboraient fièrement des tenues traditionnelles burkinabè (Faso Dan Fani, Kôkô Donda…). Ce geste vestimentaire met en lumière l'exceptionnel génie créateur des tisseuses, artisans et stylistes locaux. Ainsi, Moov Africa-ONATEL réaffirme son ancrage patriotique et magnifie le « Made in Burkina ». Et lors du petit-déjeuner, ce sont des mets traditionnels : samsa, souma, gonré, bouillie de petit mil, massa, bourmassa, babenda, piigri, benga, bissap, gingembre, téédo, et bien d'autres spécialités des terroirs qui ont été servis au public. Ragnang-Néwindé Isidore Tiemtoré, Président du Conseil d'administration (PCA) de ONATEL-SA délivrant le message du président du Faso « Tous pour le Made in Burkina. Faisons de chaque achat un acte de souveraineté, car c’est de nos champs, de nos ateliers, de nos boutiques et tables que se construit une nation débout, fière et souveraine », a déclaré Ragnang-Néwindé Isidore Tiemtoré, Président du Conseil d'administration (PCA) de ONATEL-SA, qui a délivré le message du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Il a ajouté que le peuple burkinabè « doit produire, transformer et consommer, car ce sont les trois maillons d’une même chaîne ». Deux voix masculine et féminine pour entonner le Ditanyè Dans le message du chef de l’Etat burkinabè prononcé par M. Tiemtoré, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré appelle les populations à s’approprier les objectifs des JEPPC et à combattre « la fraude, la contrebande et les fausses déclarations (qui) font rentrer à vil prix des produits qui concurrencent déloyalement ce que (les) unités (burkinabè) produisent honnêtement ». « Toutes ces pratiques affaiblissent notre production et doivent être combattues sans relâche », poursuit-il. De façon résumée, le message du chef de l’Etat invite le public à consommer la production nationale pour lui donner plus de valeur. Les salariés de Moov Africa-ONATEL fortement mobilisés pour la montée des Couleurs nationales « Le patriotisme du consommateur exige en retour l’excellence du produit, du service. En le ramenant à notre maison, nous devons proposer des produits à même de satisfaire notre clientèle », a souligné Ragnang-Néwindé Isidore Tiemtoré, Président du Conseil d'administration (PCA) de ONATEL-SA. Il a invité les travailleurs à s’aligner sur cette vision du président du Faso en donnant le meilleur d’eux-mêmes pour satisfaire la clientèle de la société. Le directeur général de Moov Africa-ONATEL, Mohamed Karim réaffirmant l'engagement de sa société à toujours accompagner les JEPPC Le directeur général de Moov Africa-ONATEL, Mohamed Karim, a signifié que l’engagement patriotique est exprimé de manière quotidienne au niveau de son entreprise. « Moov Africa favorise tout ce qui est production nationale allant de la petite, moyenne et grande entreprise. On essaie chaque fois que l’occasion se présente à une demande de prestation, de donner la préférence aux entreprises locales et nationales », a-t-il fait savoir, expliquant que cela est une façon pour l’entreprise « d’encourager les talents et le savoir-faire national ». Des travailleurs de Moov Africa-ONATEL fièrement habillés en Faso Dan Fani et Kôkô Dunda Cette dynamique d'engagement patriotique s'aligne harmonieusement avec la stratégie globale de Responsabilité Sociétale d'Entreprise (RSE) de Moov Africa-ONATEL à savoir la préférence nationale qui permet à la société de prioriser les entreprises, PME, prestataires et artisans locaux dans les processus d'achat et de commandes institutionnelles. Dans cette même vision, l’opérateur de téléphonie via la souveraineté numérique et inclusion financière déploie en continu des infrastructures Très Haut Débit (Fibre optique, 4G+) et de solutions de paiement mobile (Moov Money) permettant de digitaliser et de dynamiser le commerce et l'économie locale sur toute l'étendue du territoire. Des salariés attendant sereinement le top départ de la montée des Couleurs nationales Aussi, l’entreprise apporte un soutien au développement communautaire à travers l’accompagnement constant des grandes initiatives nationales, dont Faso Mêbo et les activités citoyennes et culturelles. Et ce, depuis la première phase des JEPPC lancée en avril 2024 où Moov Africa-ONATEL a participé activement et sans discontinuer à toutes les phases. items.title: Government wanted to ‘tilt the balance’ with new EC appointments – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: Government spokesperson, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has admitted that the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) wanted to “tilt the balance” in the composition of the Electoral Commission (EC) with the appointment of Emilia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story , Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the appointment was intended to address what he described as an imbalance in the political composition of the Commission. His comments come amid concerns raised by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) over Ms Agbenyo’s political neutrality following her appointment and swearing-in alongside Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah. The NPP has questioned her suitability for the position, citing her participation in the NDC’s campaign activities and her role as a spokesperson for the party’s manifesto committee on governance. Earlier on the show, Nana B had insisted that in the erstwhile administration, President John Mahama criticised some of the EC appointments, yet today, he “has appointed a known NDC member and we are questioning it, and you’re saying we do not have the guts to criticise you.” “It is not NPP you’re talking to, it is Ghanaians,” he added. Mr Kwakye Ofosu acknowledged that some people had legitimate concerns about her appointment but argued that her conduct in office would help address those concerns. “I have acknowledged that there are people who have legitimate concerns, but those concerns in my view will be mitigated by the conduct of madam Afi [Emelia Afi Agbenyo] herself in the role that she’s been given,” he said on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. He accused the NPP of applying double standards, arguing that the party had previously appointed people affiliated with it to state institutions. He also questioned why the political composition of the EC should remain unchanged if, as he claimed, several of its commissioners were associated with the NPP. “The other issue is that you see a Reset could also mean balancing the lopsided state institutions. Why is it acceptable for us to have a situation where out of seven commissioners who manage Ghana’s elections, almost four of them are NPPs? Why should we live with that? What is wrong with tilting the balance?” he asked. When the Top Story host asked whether tilting the balance meant appointing an NDC member to the Commission, Mr Kwakye Ofosu responded: “Yes.” The comments add to the debate over the political neutrality and independence of the EC following the appointment of the two deputy chairpersons. At their swearing-in ceremony, President John Dramani Mahama charged the new appointees to discharge their duties independently and impartially, stressing that no political party or candidate should receive preferential treatment. The NPP’s concerns centre on whether Ms Agbenyo’s previous political activities could affect public confidence in the Commission’s impartiality. The government, however, has maintained that concerns about her neutrality should be assessed in light of her conduct in office.

items.title: Olympics: Super Falcons thrash Comoros 5-0, set up Morocco clash
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Super Falcons of Nigeria secured a resounding 5-0 victory over Comoros at the Remo Stars stadium, Ikenne on Tuesday to seal a 7-0 aggregate win and reach the third round of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games qualifiers. A four-goal second-half surge sent interim coach Augustine Eguavoen-led side into the third round of the Olympics qualifiers, completing a 7–0 aggregate victory over Comoros. Inter Milan forward Toni Payne and Cruz Azul striker Uchenna Kanu both scored twice, with Christy Ucheibe also adding a penalty in Tuesday’s dominant performance over the Southern Africans ladies in Ikenne. Payne opened the scoring in the 41st minute after Kanu pounced on a mistake by the Comoros goalkeeper and squared the ball for her to finish. Nigeria led 1–0 at half-time, but lost captain Rasheedat Ajibade to an ankle injury. She was stretchered off in tears and replaced by Folashade Ijamilusi, who had an impressive show with two assists. Kanu doubled the lead in the 58th minute, heading in an Ijamilusi cross. Five minutes later, substitute Blessing Okpe dribbled past two defenders and laid the ball off for Payne, who scored her second. Ijamilusi delivered again in the 66th minute, crossing for Kanu to head home her second goal of the night. Okpe then won a penalty after being fouled in the area, and Ucheibe converted calmly in the 71st minute. Introduced for Gift Monday at half-time, Okpe finished with an assist and the run that led to the penalty. Nigeria kept clean sheets in both legs of the tie, giving interim coach Augustine Eguavoen an emphatic result as the team advances to the next round. The Super Falcons will face Morocco in the third round of the Olympics qualifier scheduled for March 2027, where victory in the two-legged tie will bring the dream of a fifth Olympics participation closer for Nigeria’s female national team The post Olympics: Super Falcons thrash Comoros 5-0, set up Morocco clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Côte d’Ivoire: des partis de l’opposition appellent à l’ouverture d’un dialogue national sur le nouvel organe électoral
items.description: Ceci est une déclaration commune des partis et groupements politique de l'opposition en Côte d'Ivoire. Ceux-ci appellent le gouvernement ivoirien à ouvrir un dialogue national sur le nouvel organe électoral. DECLARATION COMMUNE DES PRINCIPAUX PARTIS ET GROUPEMENTS POLITIQUES DE L’OPPOSITION Mardi 13 octobre 2026 Mesdames et Messieurs les journalistes, Chères concitoyennes, chers concitoyens, Les partis et groupements politiques de l’opposition ci-dessous mentionnés, réunis le vendredi 9 octobre 2026, ont décidé, d’une seule voix, d’inviter le Gouvernement ivoirien, par l’entremise de Monsieur le Premier Ministre, à ouvrir un dialogue national sur le nouvel organe électoral. À ce sujet, un courrier commun portant cette demande a été déposé à la Primature le Lundi 12 octobre 2026. Par cette démarche, nous voulons rechercher un accord sur les conditions d’organisation d’élections transparentes et apaisées, dont les résultats reflètent fidèlement la volonté du peuple ivoirien. C’est le sens de notre appel à l’opinion nationale et internationale. À deux reprises, les partis et groupements politiques de l’opposition ont répondu favorablement à l’invitation du Gouvernement concernant le nouvel organe électoral et ont honoré les rendez-vous fixés. Dans ce même esprit d’ouverture, ils attendent désormais du Gouvernement qu’il examine favorablement leur demande de dialogue national. Notre pays a trop souffert des contestations et des crises électorales. Les défaillances de l’ancienne Commission électorale indépendante, son impartialité contestée et son incapacité à établir une confiance partagée, ont contribué à ces crises. Sa disparition doit ouvrir une réforme de fond, capable d’empêcher la reproduction des mêmes difficultés. La crédibilité du futur dispositif dépendra de garanties concrètes, à savoir, des responsables compétents et indépendants, une désignation transparente et consensuelle de ses dirigeants, une autonomie effective à l’égard du pouvoir politique et un contrôle impartial de l’ensemble du processus. Elle dépendra aussi d’une liste électorale fiable, soumise à un audit indépendant et régulièrement actualisée, afin que les citoyens remplissant les conditions requises, notamment les nouveaux majeurs, puissent s’inscrire. Chaque électeur doit pouvoir voter librement et avoir l’assurance que son suffrage sera correctement compté. Nous demandons une traçabilité complète des opérations, l’accès aux procès-verbaux et la publication des résultats détaillés, bureau de vote par bureau de vote. Des recours effectifs et impartiaux doivent permettre de résoudre les différends par les voies institutionnelles. La transparence doit rendre les résultats vérifiables et réduire les motifs de contestation. Ces garanties doivent être discutées ensemble. Une présentation par le gouvernement, de décisions déjà arrêtées sans concertations avec l’opposition, ne répondrait pas à notre demande. Nous souhaitons un dialogue dans lequel les propositions puissent être examinées, les désaccords traités et un accord écrit obtenu, avant la finalisation et l’adoption des textes. Ce dialogue national doit associer le Gouvernement, les partis de la majorité et de l’opposition ainsi que les organisations de la société civile concernées choisis de manière consensuelle. La confiance électorale engage toute la nation. Elle exige une méthode inclusive et un calendrier précis. Les partis de l’opposition sont unis autour de cette exigence. Nous sommes prêts à présenter nos propositions, à écouter celles des autres participants et à travailler de bonne foi, à une solution qui protège le libre choix des citoyens. Nous appelons le Gouvernement à répondre favorablement à cette invitation et à proposer rapidement une rencontre préparatoire. Prévenir une crise électorale commence par l’établissement de règles crédibles, avant le scrutin. Nous invitons les Ivoiriennes et les Ivoiriens à soutenir cette démarche pacifique. Nous appelons également les partenaires régionaux et internationaux de la Côte d’Ivoire à encourager ce dialogue, dans le respect de la souveraineté de notre pays. Notre engagement est clair : défendre le suffrage, rechercher le consensus et préserver la paix. Le peuple ivoirien doit pouvoir choisir ses dirigeants dans les urnes, avec la certitude que son choix sera respecté. Nous vous remercions. items.title: Angry Tema Community 25 residents threaten to sleep at GWL over water shortage
items.description: Residents of Tema Community 25 and surrounding communities have threatened to occupy the head office of the Ghana Water Limited (GWL) and sleep there until a reliable water supply is restored. The residents say they have endured persistent water shortages for years, forcing many households to rely on water tankers and boreholes at high cost. They issued the warning after a previous visit to the company’s Tema office and assurances of intervention failed to improve the situation. They are demanding urgent intervention from the government and Ghana Water, warning that they would bring their families and mattresses to the company’s head office and remain there until water supply is restored. “We have given the government two weeks. If we don’t get the water, then we’re going to take action. We would come and sleep at the Ghana Water Limited office till we get water,” they warned. The residents said they had visited the company’s regional office twice and received responses but were yet to see a lasting solution that would ensure a reliable supply to all affected households. In an interview with JoyNews, one resident lamented the situation. “Since 2022, in fact, it has been an unbearable situation within this community. We’ve not been having water. We depend on tankers that supply us water almost every day,” the resident said. The resident added that the shortage had also affected four fire hydrants serving the community and surrounding areas, raising concerns about access to water during fire outbreaks. Another resident, who has lived in the community for eight years, said she had relied on borehole water throughout her stay and had invested nearly GH¢30,000 in a reverse osmosis filtration system because of concerns about water quality. She said the water crisis had also affected her rental property, which had remained vacant for a year, resulting in lost income. Other residents said some households spend between GH¢1,000 and GH¢1,200 monthly to purchase water, describing the situation as financially burdensome. They accused the water company of charging estimated bills despite the absence of water in their taps.

items.title: BoG takes financial literacy drive to Techiman, vows to protect depositors
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has reaffirmed its commitment to deepening engagement with stakeholders across the country, emphasizing collaboration and shared responsibility in sustaining Ghana’s economic stability. In its first-ever stakeholders’ engagement in Techiman, the Bono East Regional capital, the Central Bank brought its message of financial literacy, consumer protection, and inclusive dialogue directly to traders, market women, and business owners under the theme “ Strengthening Stakeholder Relations Through Dialogue and Engagement .” Speaking at the event, Director of Communications at the Bank of Ghana, Bernard Ato Otabil, explained that the initiative forms part of a broader strategy to strengthen collaboration between the Central Bank and local stakeholders. “This engagement is about inclusiveness. It’s about letting the people know the operations of the Bank of Ghana,” he said. “We want to build trust and ensure that every Ghanaian understands what we do and how it affects their daily lives.” The engagement covered a range of critical topics, including: · The role and mandate of the Bank of Ghana · Responsible borrowing and consumer protection · Dud cheques: causes, implications, and prevention · Currency education: identification and proper handling of banknotes The Regional Director of the Bank of Ghana for the Sunyani office, Lawal Abubakari, who oversees the Bono, Bono East, Ahafo, and parts of the Upper West Region, noted that the feedback received from the engagement will strengthen the bank’s output across all regions—not only in the Bono East. “The feedback we have gathered here today is invaluable. It will help us refine our approach and improve our services not just in Techiman or the Bono East Region, but across the entire country,” he said. “This is why we are committed to listening to the people. Their experiences and concerns shape the policies and interventions we design.” His remarks underscored the Bank of Ghana’s broader vision of using regional engagements as a feedback loop to enhance its operations nationwide. While participants lauded the Bank of Ghana’s decision to educate them on its operations, some expressed deep-seated concerns about their inability to identify genuine financial institutions. Many traders in the region still bear the scars of past experiences where financial institutions collapsed, taking with them monies belonging to hardworking traders. The memories of those losses have left many afraid to entrust their savings to banks. Queenmother of the Techiman Fishmongers Association, Nana Grace Tina, voiced the concerns of many when she appealed to authorities for help. “We want the authorities to help us identify reliable financial institutions that will help us do our business without fear,” she said. “We have suffered before. We don’t want to suffer again.” Responding to these concerns, Mr. Otabil offered reassurance, explaining that the Central Bank has put in place robust measures to protect depositors. “With the current measures put in place by the Central Bank, the customer is protected. No such thing can happen where customers will lose their deposits,” he assured. “We have strengthened our regulatory framework, and we continue to monitor all financial institutions to ensure compliance.” He encouraged participants to verify the status of any financial institution with the Bank of Ghana before committing their funds. The Ghana Union of Traders Association (GUTA) commended the Bank of Ghana for organizing the program and called for it to be held regularly. The Regional President of GUTA, Yeboah Asuamah Kyimeh, said the initiative would help traders understand financial inclusion and ultimately contribute to poverty alleviation. “This program is commendable. We wish it could be held intermittently to help educate traders in this area to understand the financial inclusion that will help alleviate poverty,” he said. The event concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session, where participants had the opportunity to seek clarification on various concerns, including how to identify counterfeit currency, the process for reporting dud cheques, and the steps to take when dealing with unlicensed financial institutions. Hundreds of participants showed up for the engagement, reflecting the strong appetite for financial education in the region. The Bank of Ghana says the Techiman engagement is just the beginning. The Central Bank plans to extend the dialogue to other regions across the country, ensuring that every Ghanaian, regardless of location, has access to information about the Central Bank’s role and their rights as consumers. For the traders of Techiman, the event offered not only knowledge but also hope—hope that with continued engagement and stronger regulation, their money will be safe, and their businesses will thrive.

items.title: ‘Stop the distractions’ – Akosua Manu demands answers over GH¢49.7m South Africa evacuation cost
items.description: Akosua Manu, an advisor to NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has demanded answers to questions surrounding Ghana’s GH¢49.7 million South Africa evacuation exercise, warning against shifting the public debate towards political disagreements over service passports. In a Facebook post on Tuesday, October 13, Ms Manu said the public deserved a transparent account of the expenditure, particularly in light of concerns about payment registers, alleged ghost names and discrepancies in flight records. She described the development as “an insult to the intelligence of Ghanaians”, arguing that allegations concerning Nana Boakye’s service passport did not address the substance of the financial questions. Ms Manu’s comments come amid a public disagreement involving the Majority on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee and its Deputy Ranking Member, Nana Asafo-Ayeh, over criticism of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. The Majority has accused Mr Asafo-Ayeh of pursuing a campaign of “character assassination” against the Minister. It claims the tension stems from Mr Ablakwa’s refusal to grant a service passport to Nana Boakye, popularly known as Nana B, a former NPP National Youth Organiser and now NPP 2nd Vice Chairman and former Board Chairman of the National Food Buffer Stock Company. According to the Majority, the Minister acted in accordance with a presidential directive requiring holders of diplomatic and service passports to return them. Salaga South MP Zuwera Ibrahimah Mohammed has defended the Minister’s position, arguing that public officials must operate within the law when dealing with requests for favours. Ms Manu, however, insists that the passport controversy must not displace scrutiny of the evacuation expenditure. She maintains that the records should be made available for proper examination so the public can establish how the funds were used. “If there is nothing to hide, an independent audit should be welcomed,” she said, renewing her call for accountability and insisting that the documents should provide the answers Ghanaians seek.

items.title: Lounès Magramane : qui est le nouveau directeur de cabinet de la Présidence ?
items.description: Le diplomate Lounès Magramane est le nouveau directeur de cabinet de la présidence de la République. Il a été nommé ce mardi 13 octobre par le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Le désormais ancien secrétaire général du ministère des Affaires étrangères, succède à Boualem Boualem, décédé lundi 5 octobre dans un hôpital à Genève en Suisse. Qui est le nouveau directeur de cabinet de la Présidence de la République ? Lounès Magramane, un diplomate au long parcours Né le 1er juin 1961 à Khemis El Khechna dans la wilaya de Boumerdès, Lounès Magramane , qui était en première ligne dans la gestion de la grave crise entre l’Algérie et la France de 2024 et 2025, est marié et père de trois enfants. Diplômé de l'Ecole nationale d'administration (ENA) d’Alger, section diplomatique, il maîtrise l’arabe, l’anglais et le français. Lounès Magramane, 61 ans, a un long parcours dans la diplomatie algérienne. Il commence sa carrière au ministère des Affaires étrangères en 1986 comme chef de Bureau des affaires politiques de l'Organisation de l'Unité africaine (OUA) et des mouvements de libération nationale. Un poste qu’il occupe jusqu’à 1990, avant d’être nommé ministre-conseiller à l’ambassade d'Algérie à Addis-Abeba pendant quatre ans. Puis, retour au siège du ministère des Affaires étrangères à Alger comme sous-directeur de l'Organisation de l'Unité africaine (OUA) et des Organisations régionales. En 1997, il monte en grade et prend la direction Afrique au ministère des Affaires étrangères jusqu’en 2001 et sa nomination comme ambassadeur d'Algérie à Niamey, au Niger. Après quatre ans, il revient en Algérie après sa désignation comme chef de cabinet du ministre des Affaires étrangères, puis ambassadeur conseiller auprès du ministre des AE (2007-2008), directeur général Afrique (2008-2009). De 2009 à 20015, il occupe le poste d’ambassadeur d'Algérie à Budapest (Hongrie) et de Slovénie avec résidence dans la capitale hongroise. Puis retour une nouvelle fois à Alger comme directeur général du protocole au ministère des Affaires étrangères jusqu’en 2019. Lounès Magramane, une solide expérience africaine Lounès Magramane redevient ambassadeur cette fois à La Haye aux Pays-Bas où il reste jusqu’à novembre 2021. Il occupe dans le même temps le poste représentant permanent de l'Algérie auprès de l'Organisation pour l'Interdiction des Armes Chimiques (l'OIAC) à La Haye, et de gouverneur du CFC (Fonds Commun pour les produits de base) à Amsterdam. En novembre 2021, il est nommé ambassadeur d'Algérie à Londres et représentant permanent de l'Algérie auprès de l'Organisation Maritime Internationale. Le 6 juin 2023, il est désigné secrétaire général du ministère des Affaires étrangères jusqu’à ce mardi 13 octobre. Lounès Magramane a fait partie des délégations algériennes au titre de médiation dans le conflit interne du Niger (1998) et dans le processus de règlement du conflit Ethiopie-Erythrée 1999-2000n, et participé à plusieurs réunions ministérielles, au sommet des chefs d'Etats de l'OUA et de l'Union Africaine de 1988 à 2000. Lounès Magramane est décoré du commandeur de l'Ordre du mérite de la République du Niger et de la Croix médiane de l'Ordre du Mérite de Hongrie, selon sa biographie officielle. items.title: Formula 1 to return to Africa with Rwanda Grand Prix in early 2030s
items.description: Formula 1 will return to Africa for the first time since 1993 after signing a 10-year agreement with Rwanda to host the Formula 1 African Grand Prix in the early 2030s. The race, presented by Visit Rwanda, will be held at a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, about 40 kilometres south of the capital, Kigali. The agreement was announced on Tuesday, October 13, with the circuit expected to be completed early in the next decade. The track will be developed to meet FIA Grade 1 standards, the highest required for hosting Formula 1 races, as part of a wider project led by the Rwanda Development Board. Located close to the new Kigali International Airport, the circuit will use the area’s natural landscape and elevation changes to create a challenging racing experience. Beyond Formula 1, the venue is expected to host other motorsport competitions, international events, conferences and entertainment activities. Formula 1 last raced on the African continent at South Africa’s Kyalami circuit in 1993. The return to Rwanda will mark a major step in the sport’s efforts to expand its global presence. Formula 1 says Africa already has more than 100 million fans, with almost 60 per cent of fans in key sub-Saharan African markets under the age of 35. Formula 1 president and chief executive Stefano Domenicali described the agreement as a landmark moment for the sport. “Africa has always been part of Formula 1’s future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact,” he said. Domenicali added that the project was intended to deliver benefits beyond the race weekend through tourism, investment, skills development and opportunities for local businesses. Rwanda President Paul Kagame said the agreement would give African fans the opportunity to experience the sport on the continent while creating opportunities for young people. “Rwanda is proud to host the Formula 1 African Grand Prix, and to share this moment with more than 100 million fans across Africa, many of them young people who deserve to see the sport at home and to see themselves in it: as engineers, technicians, entrepreneurs and, one day, drivers,” he said. Kagame added that the 10-year partnership was an investment in Rwanda’s future, with the circuit and airport expected to support jobs, tourism and business development. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem also welcomed the agreement, describing the return of Formula 1 to Africa as a historic moment. He said the FIA would work with Formula 1 and its partners to ensure the new circuit meets international standards while helping develop motorsport talent across the continent. Further details, including the inaugural race date, construction milestones and race-weekend plans, are expected to be announced later. The Rwanda Grand Prix will make Africa the final inhabited continent to be represented on the Formula 1 calendar once the race begins.

items.title: Session parlementaire 2026-2027 : cinq propositions de commissions d’enquête à l’étude
items.description: À l’ouverture de la session ordinaire unique 2026-2027, ce mardi 13 octobre, le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Ousmane Sonko, a annoncé le dépôt de propositions de résolution visant à créer cinq commissions d’enquête parlementaires. Les dossiers concernés portent notamment sur les blocs pétroliers et gaziers, la lutte contre les inondations, les fonds spéciaux de certaines institutions publiques, des programmes financés par Banco Santander et la protection des données personnelles dans le secteur de la santé. Cinq dossiers sont soumis à l’attention des députés. À l’occasion de l’ouverture de la session ordinaire unique 2026-2027, Ousmane Sonko a annoncé des initiatives visant à examiner plusieurs questions d’intérêt public liées à la gestion des ressources naturelles, à l’utilisation des fonds publics et à la protection des données personnelles. La création de ces commissions reste toutefois soumise à la procédure parlementaire. Les propositions de résolution devront être examinées par le Bureau de l’Assemblée nationale pour en vérifier la recevabilité, avant l’avis du Garde des Sceaux, ministre de la Justice. Les blocs pétroliers et gaziers dans le viseur Le premier dossier concerne les conditions d’attribution et de reprise des blocs pétroliers et gaziers, notamment ceux de Saint-Louis et de Kayar. Les travaux envisagés pourraient porter sur les différentes étapes de ces opérations et les acteurs concernés, parmi lesquels Petro-Tim, Kosmos Energy et Woodside. Cette initiative place la gestion des ressources naturelles au cœur des questions que les députés souhaitent examiner. Le Plan décennal de lutte contre les inondations Le deuxième dossier porte sur le Plan décennal de lutte contre les inondations. Une commission d’enquête pourrait permettre d’examiner ce programme, consacré à la prévention et à la gestion des risques d’inondation. Les fonds spéciaux de trois institutions publiques La gestion des fonds spéciaux de la Primature, du Haut Conseil des collectivités territoriales (HCCT) et du Conseil économique, social et environnemental (CESE) constitue le troisième dossier. La période concernée s’étend de 2012 à 2026. L’enquête envisagée porterait ainsi sur quatorze années de gestion de ces fonds au sein des trois institutions. Trois programmes financés par Banco Santander Le quatrième dossier concerne plusieurs programmes financés par Banco Santander, pour un montant cumulé d’environ 227,34 milliards de FCFA. Il s’agit du programme d’acquisition d’équipements agricoles et de construction d’entrepôts, confié à INTERMAQ 2012 SL, pour 85,51 milliards de FCFA ; du Projet d’appui structurel à la stratégie d’aménagement numérique du territoire (PASSANT), confié à LITEYCA SL, pour 50 milliards de FCFA ; et du projet d’électrification rurale confié à AEE POWER EPC, pour environ 91,83 milliards de FCFA. Ces trois programmes figurent parmi les dossiers pour lesquels une enquête parlementaire est proposée. La protection des données personnelles en question Le cinquième dossier porte sur la sécurisation des données personnelles nationales dans le cadre du protocole d’accord signé le 13 mars 2026 entre le ministère de la Santé et les États-Unis d’Amérique dans le domaine de la santé. L’examen envisagé concerne les enjeux liés à la protection des données personnelles dans le cadre de cet accord. Des propositions soumises à la procédure parlementaire La mise en place des cinq commissions d’enquête n’est pas encore actée. Les propositions de résolution devront d’abord être examinées par le Bureau de l’Assemblée nationale, puis suivre la procédure prévue, notamment avec l’avis du Garde des Sceaux, ministre de la Justice. Les dossiers pourront ensuite être inscrits à l’ordre du jour de la session ordinaire unique 2026-2027, conformément aux procédures applicables. Ces initiatives parlementaires portent sur cinq domaines distincts, allant de la gestion des ressources naturelles et des fonds publics au financement de projets d’infrastructures et à la protection des données personnelles. C.G.D
