items.title: Les lycéens de nouveau dans la rue : la mobilisation évolue-t-elle ?
items.description: Acte V de la mobilisation lycéenne en France : lycéens, étudiants et enseignants ont battu le pavé dans toute la France. Le ministère fait état d’un « recul » des blocages de lycées, avec 214 établissements concernés ce mardi, contre 800 mardi dernier. Selon le ministère de l’Intérieur, 161 500 personnes ont manifesté en France, dont 41 500 à Paris. Des tensions ont éclaté en fin de cortège, près de l’esplanade des Invalides. Greta Thunberg est venue manifester ce matin en solidarité avec les lycéens, devant le lycée Paul-Éluard de Saint-Denis. On revient sur cet acte V de la mobilisation lycéenne : où en est-on ? Y a-t-il un essoufflement du mouvement ? Évolue-t-il ? Est-il appelé à durer ? La réponse politique est-elle à la hauteur des attentes, alors que s’ouvrent à l’Assemblée nationale les discussions autour du budget ?

items.title: De Léopold Senghor à Bassirou Diomaye : L’âge du pouvoir au Sénégal
items.description: De Léopold Sédar Senghor à Bassirou Diomaye Faye, cinq hommes, aux parcours différents ont dirigé le Sénégal. À 44 ans, l’actuel chef de l’État est le plus jeune Président de l’histoire du Sénégal, tandis qu’Abdoulaye Wade en est le doyen, à 73 ans. L’âge moyen d’accession au pouvoir, au Sénégal, s’établit à environ 55 ans. Mais cette moyenne n’est pas homogène. Deux présidents ont accédé à la magistrature suprême avant 46 ans, deux autres autour de la cinquantaine, tandis qu’un seul réalise son ambition présidentielle à 73 ans. Léopold Sédar Senghor Né le 9 octobre 1906 à Joal, Léopold Sédar Senghor accède à la présidence en septembre 1960. Il a alors 53 ans. Poète, agrégé de grammaire, Senghor arrive au pouvoir avec une expérience avérée de la vie publique. Son parcours s’est construit avant l’indépendance, notamment au sein des institutions politiques françaises, puis dans les responsabilités exercées au Sénégal. Il incarne une génération de dirigeants dont la trajectoire s’est forgée dans les combats ayant accompagné la décolonisation. Il est le premier président du Sénégal indépendant et demeure à la tête du pays jusqu’à sa démission, le 31 décembre 1980. Abdou Diouf Né le 7 septembre 1935 à Louga, Abdou Diouf accède à la présidence le 1er janvier 1981, à la suite de la démission de Senghor. Il a alors 45 ans. Haut fonctionnaire de formation, il a notamment été directeur de cabinet du président Senghor, secrétaire général de la présidence, ministre, puis Premier ministre à partir de 1970. Cette progression lui permet d’accumuler une expérience importante de l’appareil d’État avant même d’accéder à la magistrature suprême. Il restera président jusqu’en avril 2000. Me Abdoulaye Wade Né le 29 mai 1926, il devient président le 1er avril 2000, à l’âge de 73 ans. Avocat de formation, son accession à la présidence montre que le sommet de l’État requiert parfois de l’abnégation et de la détermination. À 73 ans, Wade devient le président le plus âgé au moment de sa prise de fonction parmi les cinq chefs d’État sénégalais. L’arrivée de Me Abdoulaye Wade au pouvoir symbolise également une nouvelle séquence institutionnelle, après près de quatre décennies de présidence socialiste (Diouf et Senghor). Macky Sall Né le 11 décembre 1961 à Fatick, Macky Sall accède à la présidence le 2 avril 2012, à l’âge de 50 ans. Ingénieur géologue de formation, il exerce plusieurs responsabilités gouvernementales, notamment plusieurs fois ministre, avant de devenir Premier ministre de 2004 à 2007 et président de l’Assemblée nationale en 2007. À 50 ans, Macky Sall arrive donc au pouvoir avec une expérience déjà établie des institutions et de l’exercice des responsabilités publiques. Son parcours symbolise un rude apprentissage au sein de l’appareil d’État. Bassirou Diomaye Faye Né le 25 mars 1980, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye prête serment le 2 avril 2024, à l’âge de 44 ans. Il devient le cinquième président de la République du Sénégal et le plus jeune à accéder à cette fonction depuis l’indépendance. Inspecteur des Impôts et des Domaines de formation, il incarne un renouvellement générationnel au sommet de l’État. Son élection ouvre ainsi une nouvelle séquence de l’histoire politique sénégalaise, celle d’un président arrivé au pouvoir avant 45 ans. À 44 ans, il se situe nettement en dessous de l’âge moyen d’accession au pouvoir de ses quatre prédécesseurs. O.BA

items.title: Tinubu to Judiciary: Seal loopholes criminals exploit to escape justice
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA– PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has asked the Judiciary to dismantle procedural loopholes and flawed prosecution tactics that allow offenders to escape justice, warning that no well-connected individual should be able to manipulate technicalities to evade the law. The President spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the annual EFCC/NJI Capacity Building Workshop for Judges and Justices. He was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Tinubu urged the judiciary to interrogate existing statutory frameworks in view of emerging financial crimes. “Probe prosecution strategies, dismantle outdated precedents, and seal procedural gaps that politically exposed persons and organised crime actors exploit to delay or frustrate trial,” he stated. He demanded an aggressive overhaul of the justice system to ensure that no well-connected individual can manipulate technicalities to evade the full, crushing weight of the law. The President, who was represented by the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, warned that financial and economic crimes pose an existential threat to Nigeria, adding that corruption has no respect for status and spares no arm of government. He said framing the anti-corruption campaign as purely an executive agenda is a fundamental error because compromised public services equally affect the executive, legislature, judiciary, and ordinary citizens. “Corruption is a battle for the nation’s collective survival. We must no longer permit legal pyrotechnics and procedural pedantry to shelter criminality. The Bench is not merely a mechanical arbiter of rules, but an active guardian of moral order and social equity. “Law is, by design, an instrument of social engineering; it must invariably prioritise the public good over narrow, selfish interests shielded by technical manoeuvres. Our courts must embody the spirit, and not just the arid letter, of the law,” Tinubu said. He maintained that there will be no meaningful progress in uprooting graft “without an independent, progressive, and reform-minded Bench.” Digital-age crimes Tinubu commended the EFCC for convening the 8th edition of the Judges and Justices Workshop, themed “Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Financial Crimes in a Digital Age.” He described the workshop as timely and necessary in fostering the institutional cohesion required to confront corruption’s changing architecture in Nigeria. “My Lords, we confront a rapidly shifting criminal landscape. Technology has amplified the audacity and reach of illicit actors, ushering in sophisticated crimes driven by destructive ingenuity. The rise of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence has introduced unprecedented layers of complexity to traditional illicit activities. “Because these modern crimes constantly mutate, law enforcement and judicial authorities must continuously build capacity to adapt and respond effectively,” he added. The President urged the judiciary to adapt to shifting dynamics of financial crime, stressing that realigning the nation’s investigative and prosecutorial strategies is critical to preventing institutional obsolescence. Tinubu said the country was already on the right trajectory, citing the EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and recovering virtual assets. “The EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and its commendable strides in recovering virtual assets are highly reassuring. The agency has recovered billions of naira in cryptocurrency investment-related fraud cases. “In 2025, the agency secured the forfeiture of $22,417.91 (Twenty-Two Thousand, Four Hundred and Seventeen Dollars, Ninety-One Cents) worth of Bitcoin; 1,001,301.87 USDT (One Million, One Thousand, Three Hundred and One USDT and Eighty-Seven Cents) in digital assets; and US$5.6 million linked to the CBEX scheme, while 192 foreigners arrested for cyber-terrorism and cryptocurrency fraud were successfully prosecuted and deported afterwards,” he said. He said the EFCC’s actions show an agency that is proactive, forward-looking and resolved not to be outpaced by technological innovation, while the judiciary must complement law enforcement by rapidly upscaling its capacity. Tinubu acknowledged the Chief Justice of Nigeria’s efforts in reforming the judiciary and pledged the full support of the executive to ensure the judiciary is adequately equipped for justice delivery in the digital age. Earlier, Chief Justice of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, said the 8th edition of the event reflects the commitment of the NJI and EFCC to sustain efforts aimed at addressing challenges confronting stakeholders in Nigeria’s justice system. She said the trend in technology has impacted how digital evidence is obtained and recorded, noting that effective administration of criminal justice in the digital era requires firm and disciplined case management, which capacity-building programmes such as the EFCC and NJI collaboration aim to strengthen. The CJN noted that sustained judicial education and capacity development in the justice sector was yielding positive results, with improved conduct of judicial officers, especially judges, in case management and the dispensation of justice in recent years. Senate Committee Chairman on Anti-Corruption and Financial Crimes, Sen. Emmanuel Udende, said the timing of the workshop was apt given the increasing sophistication of financial crimes and corruption, particularly cases involving politically exposed persons, which directly impact timely case management and the dispensation of justice. He assured stakeholders that the National Assembly remained committed to supporting the enhancement of the war against corruption and financial crimes in Nigeria through proactive legislation. Minister of Justice and Attorney General of the Federation, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, represented by the Director of Public Prosecution, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo, urged synergy among stakeholders in addressing emerging challenges in Nigeria’s fight against corruption, stating that one arm of government alone could not effectively address the problem. He urged judicial officers, especially judges and lawyers, to leverage opportunities provided during the workshop to enhance their capacities to make investigation more thorough and prosecution more diligent. In his welcome address, Administrator of the National Judicial Institute, Justice Babatunde Adejumo, said the collaboration between the EFCC and the NJI in enhancing the capacity of judicial officers has become an integral part of government’s efforts to frontally tackle the dynamics and scale of financial crimes in the digital age. He said the presence of the Vice President at the event was a practical demonstration of the commitment of the Tinubu administration to boost Nigeria’s war against corruption. Executive Chairman of the EFCC, Mr Ola Olukoyede, said the event was a national imperative that has become an important component of the annual programme of both the EFCC and the NJI. He said the commission under his leadership was reform-minded and has recorded unprecedented convictions as well as financial recoveries over the past three years, assuring transparent and judicious handling of recovered money and property. Olukoyede also regretted the impact of advanced technology on financial crimes and other forms of corruption, noting that digital innovation was fast outpacing legal instruments and provisions for prosecution. items.title: Mahama says Ghana is safer today as he commissions 85-bed ward at Police Hospital
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has said Ghana is safer today than it was in the past, attributing the improvement to the efforts of the Ghana Police Service in maintaining peace and security across the country. The President made the remarks during the commissioning of an 85-bed ward at the Ghana Police Hospital in Accra, named after Mr Christian Tetteh Yohuno, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP). The commissioning of the three-storey facility formed part of activities marking the Golden Jubilee celebration of the Police Hospital. The ward is equipped with modern healthcare facilities. President Mahama commended Mr Yohuno for his leadership and dedication to ensuring peace and security nationwide. “Our country is safer today than it was before,” the President said. The President cited the testimony of a bus driver, who noted that commercial vehicles can now travel at any hour of the night without fear of highway robbery. “He (the driver) says today, any time the bus is full, even at 2:00 am, they take off because the roads are safer.” He said the country had also witnessed a reduction in unresolved murder cases and praised the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service for its efforts in crime detection and investigations. President Mahama further commended the Police Intelligence Directorate and the Police Cyber Unit for their contributions to national security. “Indeed, this Police Administration is doing a yeoman’s job, and as Commander-in-Chief and President of the Republic, I want to express the gratitude of our nation to all of you, and urge you to keep up the good work,” he said. The President noted that Ghana continued to be recognised as one of the safest countries in West Africa, making it an attractive destination for visitors and investors. “It’s no wonder everybody wants to visit Ghana because they say it’s the safest country in the whole of West Africa, and I can assure you that we’ll continue to provide you with the logistics that you need to continue to do your job.” The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, said President Mahama’s commitment to improving healthcare infrastructure and enhancing the welfare of security personnel continued to leave a lasting impact on the nation. He said the new facility was a testament to the President’s determination to build a stronger and more inclusive Ghana. The Inspector-General of Police expressed gratitude to President Mahama for his continuous support for the Police Service and the welfare of its personnel. He assured the President that the Police Administration would continue to implement initiatives aimed at improving the health, welfare and operational effectiveness of officers.

items.title: Senate bill to decriminalise attempted suicide passes second reading
items.description: The Senate on Tuesday passed for second reading a bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and strengthen support for survivors during plenary. The bill, sponsored by Sen. Asuquo Ekpenyong (Cross River South) seeks to establish a legal and institutional framework for suicide prevention, treatment and support for people experiencing psychological distress. Leading the debate for the bill, Ekpenyong said Nigeria’s existing laws presented conflicting approaches to attempted suicide, with mental health legislation recognising it as a psychiatric emergency while criminal laws prescribed punishment. “At the heart of this bill is a simple question: when a Nigerian survives a suicide attempt, should the first response of the state be prosecution or protection?” he asked. According to him, the National Mental Health Act recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate intervention, while Sections 327 of the Criminal Code and 231 of the Penal Code exposes survivors to criminal punishment. Ekpenyong said the bill would resolve the contradiction by prioritising prevention, treatment and the preservation of life. He argued that criminalisation could discourage people experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help and cause families to conceal suicide attempts for fear of stigma or prosecution. According to him, such practices can delay intervention and undermine reliable data collection, weakening national suicide-prevention efforts. The senator said decriminalising attempted suicide would neither legalise nor encourage suicide, adding that the bill focused on protecting survivors and ensuring access to timely medical care. He said the proposed legislation would establish coordinated prevention services, including crisis helplines, referral pathways and follow-up support for people who survived suicide attempts. Ekpenyong added that the bill would strengthen public education and train healthcare workers, law-enforcement personnel, teachers and emergency responders to recognise warning signs and connect at-risk individuals with appropriate services. He said families affected by suicide or attempted suicide would also require access to psychosocial support, while improved data collection and research would help the government develop effective prevention policies. The senator said the bill would provide an institutional and funding framework for implementing suicide-prevention services, stressing that decriminalisation without accessible care would be incomplete. He added that the committee stage would allow lawmakers to harmonise the proposed legislation with the Criminal Code, Penal Code, National Mental Health Act and relevant state laws. Other lawmakers who took turns to support the bill argued that attempted suicide should be treated primarily as a mental health concern requiring professional care rather than criminal punishment. They said that people experiencing severe emotional distress needed medical attention and support, adding that detention or imprisonment would not address the underlying causes of their conditions. They stressed that suicide prevention required coordinated action involving healthcare professionals, educational institutions, families, law enforcement agencies and relevant government institutions. The proposed legislation, according to them, will provide an opportunity for public consultation and professional contributions before the Senate takes further legislative action. Senate President Godswill Akpabio subsequently put the bill to a voice vote, and it was passed for second reading, and thereafter referred the bill to the committee on health and Judiciary, human rights and legal matters The post Senate bill to decriminalise attempted suicide passes second reading appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Assainissement de Conakry : Vivo Energy Guinée fait un don en carburant à travers la Chambre des Mines de Guinée
items.description: Dans le cadre de ses engagements en matière de responsabilité sociétale, Vivo Energy Guinée apporte son soutien aux efforts d'assainissement de la capitale à travers un don de carburant, destiné à l'Agence Nationale de l'Assainissement et de la Salubrité Publique (ANASP). Cette contribution s'inscrit dans une initiative de solidarité coordonnée par la Chambre des Mines de Guinée (CMG), en réponse à la situation d'urgence consécutive au drame de Dar-es-Salam et à l’appel à la mobilisation de Monsieur le Premier Ministre. Conakry, le 7 octobre 2026 – Vivo Energy Guinée, entreprise spécialisée dans la distribution et la commercialisation des carburants et lubrifiants de marque Shell en Guinée sous licence, œuvre pour soutenir les communautés locales. Sa contribution à travers la remise officielle d’un don de carburant vise à renforcer les moyens logistiques nécessaires au transport des déchets de Conakry vers le nouveau site de Kouria, faciliter le désengorgement des zones de transit et de transfert et soutenir la continuité des opérations d'assainissement. La cérémonie de remise s'est tenue au siège de Vivo Energy Guinée, où le Directeur Général, M. Massamba Toure, accompagné des membres de son Comité de Direction, a accueilli Mme Fatoumata Binta Diallo, Cheffe de Cabinet de la Primature, et M. Thierno Souleymane Bah, Conseiller chargé de la Coordination interministérielle et du Suivi des réformes, représentant le Premier ministre. L’équipe de la chambre des Mines représenté par M. le Directeur Exécutif M. François Phopho Kamano a marqué son implication par sa présence, qui a permis de procéder par la voie privilégiée, à la remise du don de carburant effectuée lors de cette rencontre, à l’endroit du Directeur Général de l'ANASP M. Mamoudou Diané. Un engagement sociétal au service des communautés Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le Directeur Général de Vivo Energy Guinée, M. Massamba Toure, a souligné que cette contribution traduit la volonté de l'entreprise d'apporter une réponse concrète aux défis auxquels font face les communautés. « Pour Vivo Energy, la responsabilité sociétale fait partie de notre manière de travailler, avec sécurité, respect de l'environnement et le souci des communautés qui nous accueillent. C'est dans cet esprit, et par solidarité, que nous avons répondu à la sollicitation en appuyant les actions de l'Agence nationale de l'assainissement et de la salubrité publique, l'ANASP» Il a également réaffirmé la volonté de Vivo Energy Guinée de demeurer un partenaire engagé auprès des institutions et des communautés, soulignant l'importance du dialogue et de la collaboration entre les secteurs public et privé pour relever ensemble les défis du pays. Une mobilisation collective portée par la Chambre des Mines de Guinée Cette contribution s'inscrit dans la continuité de la mobilisation engagée par la Chambre des Mines de Guinée dès la fin du mois de septembre, en réponse à l'appel des autorités du pays. En réceptionnant le don au nom de la Chambre des Mines de Guinée, son Directeur Exécutif, M. François Phopho Kamano, a salué la contribution de Vivo Energy Guinée à cet effort collectif. Au nom du Président du Conseil d'Administration, il a exprimé sa gratitude envers l'entreprise, soulignant que cette mobilisation traduit l'engagement sociétal des membres de la Chambre et leur volonté d'accompagner les pouvoirs publics. Un appui logistique pour renforcer les opérations d'assainissement Le Directeur Général de l'ANASP, M. Mamoudou Diané, a mis en avant l'importance de cet appui pour assurer la poursuite des opérations de gestion des déchets, dans un contexte où la fermeture de la décharge de Dar-es-Salam a profondément affecté le dispositif d'assainissement de Conakry. En s'exprimant au nom du Ministre en charge de l'Assainissement, il a salué la réponse apportée par les acteurs économiques à l'appel des autorités et adressé ses remerciements à Vivo Energy Guinée, à ses collaborateurs ainsi qu'à la Chambre des Mines de Guinée pour leur contribution. La Primature salue l'engagement du secteur privé dans l'effort national d'assainissement Monsieur Thierno Souleymane Bah, Conseiller chargé de la Coordination interministérielle et du Suivi des réformes, a exprimé la reconnaissance du Gouvernement envers Vivo Energy Guinée et la Chambre des Mines de Guinée pour leur mobilisation. Il a rappelé que cet élan de solidarité fait suite à l'appel lancé par le Chef du Gouvernement au lendemain du drame de Dar-es-Salam, soulignant la nécessité d'une action concertée entre les pouvoirs publics et les acteurs économiques pour faire face aux défis d'assainissement de la capitale. La présence de la délégation de la Primature à cette cérémonie témoigne de l'importance accordée à la mobilisation du secteur privé dans la réponse nationale à cette situation d'urgence. Une contribution au service de l'intérêt général Au-delà de la réponse immédiate à cette situation d'urgence, cette initiative illustre l'importance de la collaboration entre les institutions publiques et le secteur privé face aux enjeux environnementaux et sanitaires. À travers ce don et ses engagements en matière de responsabilité sociétale, Vivo Energy Guinée réaffirme sa volonté de soutenir les communautés, de contribuer à l'amélioration de leur cadre de vie et de participer durablement au développement de la Guinée.

items.title: 2027: Fubara playing active role in Rainbow Coalition – Wike
items.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team. Wike stated this during a media chat in Abuja on Tuesday, dismissing insinuations that Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers has been sidelined in the political architecture of the state. According to him, the governor remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team. Addressing questions about Fubara’s current status and quiet disposition, Wike maintained that the governor’s perceived silence does not equate to exclusion or unhappiness. “Fubara has not been pushed aside. If you know him, he’s been a very quiet person. “He is fully a member of the Rainbow Coalition and fully playing his part in efforts to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027,” he said. The minister revealed that the governor recently hosted a crucial, high-level strategic meeting at his residence attended by key stakeholders, underscoring his active involvement in the state’s political direction. “Do you know what it takes to hold a meeting in his house? For everybody to be there? “What matters most to Gov. Fubara is ensuring that his political family retains its influence and power moving forward,” he said. Speaking as the campaign coordinator for Rivers, Wike said lists of campaign committee members have been duly submitted, with Fubara slated to serve as one of the primary leaders. Reflecting on past political tensions in the state, Wike blamed external actors and ungrateful elements, including certain opposition governors for trying to drive a wedge between him and Fubara for political mileage. He, however, noted that despite external attempts to exploit the situation, mutual forgiveness and reconciliation have prevailed. Wike also touched on speculation regarding Fubara’s future political trajectory after his tenure, including potential federal appointments. While noting that he does not possess the constitutional prerogative to nominate ministers, Wike maintained an optimistic outlook on the governor’s standing. Wike reiterated that speculations regarding friction between him and the governor are unfounded, stressing that both leaders were actively working together to safeguard the state’s political stability. He explained that the Rainbow Coalition in River was engineered to unite different political factions across party lines—including members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and other groups. He added that the goal was to champion a unified agenda under Tinubu and avoid destructive litigations that previously plagued the state. When pressed on how offices and candidacies were being shared among coalition members, Wike defended the strategy as a display of high-level political ingenuity that respects the peculiarities of different areas while maintaining team solidarity. “When you talk about politicians that agree to form an umbrella, the umbrella does not mean that all the candidates will be one party. “We look at the peculiarities of areas, and say, listen, all of us are together and all of us are supporters of Mr President,” he said. The post 2027: Fubara playing active role in Rainbow Coalition – Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: STPT: ‘Sudan’s warring parties bypass sanctions through business networks’
items.description: A new report by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker urges international governments to target the commercial networks and overseas partners sustaining the war. Sudan’s warring parties continue to circumvent international sanctions through overseas business networks, associated companies and alternative arms suppliers, according to a new report by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker (STPT) . The report, Bypassing Sanctions, Sustaining the War Economy , published in October 2026, examines sanctions imposed since the war began in April 2023. It finds that restrictions have disrupted some financial and procurement channels but have failed to dismantle the wider networks financing the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The assessment identifies gaps in sanctions targeting SAF-linked companies, including the military-owned Zadna International Company for Investment, which it says has shifted much of its business towards Egypt and Gulf states and positioned itself to benefit from post-war reconstruction. The report also traces how the RSF-linked Al Junaid conglomerate generates revenue through gold trading networks, including routes that move gold from Sudan through South Sudan to the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Meanwhile, the report documents efforts by the SAF to secure alternative weapons suppliers, including Pakistan, and to develop domestic arms production using imported materials that can be harder to track. However, the authors caution that evidence of alternative procurement routes does not, by itself, prove that sanctions caused these shifts. The STPT argues that targeting individual companies is insufficient when their subsidiaries, joint ventures and commercial partners remain outside sanctions regimes. It urges governments to coordinate designations, strengthen enforcement and engage regional partners, particularly Egypt and Gulf states, to disrupt the networks sustaining the war. The report concludes that sanctions alone cannot end the conflict and must form part of a broader political strategy, alongside stronger regional cooperation and measures to limit harm to civilians. The Black Queens followed up their 3-0 first-leg win with a commanding 7-0 victory over Mauritius in Sekondi to comfortably advance to the final qualifying round. Their reward is a reunion with Zambia, the same side that denied Ghana qualification for the Paris 2024 Olympic Games after the two teams met in the final qualifying round. items.title: Football : YellowBet soutient la détection des jeunes talents de Foot Élite à Conakry
items.description: La première édition du tournoi de détection des jeunes talents, organisée par Foot Élite à l’initiative de l’ancien international guinéen Fodé Mansaré, a été lancée ce mardi 13 octobre 2026 au stade de Coléah, à Conakry. Sponsorisé par YellowBet Guinée, ce rendez-vous réunit de jeunes footballeurs issus de plusieurs académies du pays, en présence de recruteurs venus notamment de France. Jusqu’au 17 octobre prochain, les participants auront l’occasion de démontrer leurs qualités techniques et leur potentiel, dans l’espoir d’attirer l’attention de professionnels du recrutement. Parmi eux figure Boudjemaa Sharaf, recruteur de l’US Nancy, club évoluant en deuxième division française, qui a assisté aux premières rencontres de la compétition. À l’issue de cette première journée, le recruteur français s’est dit satisfait de ses premières observations, tout en soulignant que les jeunes joueurs avaient besoin d’un peu de temps pour se libérer sur le terrain. « Pour l’instant, ça se passe bien. Les joueurs sont un tout petit peu timides au commencement, mais c’est souvent comme ça. C’est une bonne impression pour l’instant », a-t-il confié. Pour sa première visite en Guinée, Boudjemaa Sharaf affirme ne pas rechercher un profil prédéfini. Son objectif est plutôt de repérer les joueurs dont les qualités pourraient répondre aux attentes de son club. « On cherche de tout. Il n’y a pas de profil particulier. S’il y a un joueur qui est bon, qui nous intéresse, on va le remarquer, le suivre et le faire venir », a-t-il expliqué. Le recruteur a également invité les jeunes footballeurs à persévérer dans leurs efforts et à continuer de travailler pour progresser. « Qu’ils continuent à travailler, qu’ils s’accrochent. Tout est possible dans la vie », a-t-il lancé, tout en saluant le potentiel footballistique de la Guinée. Fodé Mansaré veut offrir de nouvelles perspectives aux jeunes talents À l’origine de cette initiative, l’ancien international guinéen Fodé Mansaré entend rapprocher les jeunes footballeurs du pays des recruteurs susceptibles de leur ouvrir les portes du football professionnel. La présence de professionnels étrangers représente, à ses yeux, une étape importante dans la concrétisation de cette ambition. « Je suis très content que notre ami soit là, parce que c’est ça qu’on attendait depuis un bon moment. Pour organiser un tournoi ici, c’est tellement compliqué, c’est difficile », a-t-il reconnu. Pour l’ancien international, la réussite de cette première édition ne se mesurera pas uniquement au nombre de joueurs inscrits ou de recruteurs présents, mais surtout aux opportunités concrètes qui pourront en découler. « Si on arrive à détecter un joueur, voire deux ou trois, c’est le plus important », a-t-il insisté, espérant que cette compétition permettra à certains jeunes Guinéens de franchir un cap dans leur carrière. Au-delà de la détection, Fodé Mansaré souhaite également mettre en lumière le potentiel des joueurs formés en Afrique et rappeler que les talents ne se trouvent pas exclusivement en Europe. « On a des talents ici aussi. Ce n’est pas parce qu’on attend l’Europe, l’Europe, l’Europe qu’on doit oublier qu’il y a des talents chez nous », a-t-il souligné, invitant les jeunes à faire leurs preuves sur le terrain et à faire preuve de sérieux dans leur progression. YellowBet, un partenaire de la promotion du football jeune Le soutien de YellowBet Guinée constitue un apport important pour l’organisation de cette première édition du tournoi de détection de Foot Élite. En accompagnant cette initiative, le sponsor contribue à offrir une vitrine aux jeunes footballeurs guinéens et à favoriser leur mise en relation avec des professionnels du recrutement. Prévu jusqu’au 17 octobre, ce tournoi ambitionne ainsi de faire émerger de nouveaux talents et de leur donner l’occasion de se faire remarquer au-delà des frontières guinéennes.

items.title: State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days
items.description: The detention of six journalists from fact-checking platform Matsda2sh was renewed for 15 days on Tuesday evening, pending further investigations, according to their lawyers. The renewal was ordered by the Supreme State Security Prosecution during today’s hearing in Case 8083/2026. The journalists Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira, Abdallah Kadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal are being investigated in the case, registered with the Supreme State Security Prosecution, and were questioned again by prosecutors in sessions on Tuesday. The journalists’ lawyers told Mada Masr that questioning began around 1 pm and continued into the evening at the prosecution’s headquarters in the Fifth Settlement. The sessions revisited previous lines of questioning, including questioning about wages, the managerial structure of the platform and the way work was organized, with no new evidence presented to the journalists. All six journalists have been held at Badr 1 Prison since they were brought before the prosecution early last week. Their lawyers said they are due to receive their first family visits starting Thursday, as well as to be granted dedicated time for exercise. Security forces arrested the six Matsda2sh journalists in the span of24 hours during a campaign launched on September 28 which targeted the fact-checking platform’s team across several governorates. Their whereabouts remained unknown for five days, during which they were denied access to their lawyers and prevented from contacting their families, in violation of the counterterrorism law under which they were detained, according to EIPR . They appeared before the Supreme State Security Prosecution on October 4 when investigations began. The prosecution is investigating the six journalists for several offenses, including joining a terrorist group, spreading false news, misusing social media and receiving foreign funding. Several journalists told prosecutors during their interrogations that they had been subjected to torture and forced to record video footage in custody of themselves reading fabricated confessions, according to the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose legal team is leading their defense. The Journalists Syndicate subsequently filed a complaint with the prosecutor general, calling for an investigation into allegations that the journalists were tortured at National Security Agency facilities before being brought before the prosecution. The Interior Ministry denied the allegations two hours after the syndicate issued its statement. Three of the detained journalists were referred to the Forensic Medicine Authority on October 6. The prosecution said the following day that forensic reports found no injuries on their bodies or signs of violence having been used against them. EIPR responded to the prosecutor’s statement by noting that prosecutors had refused to hear the journalists’ testimony as victims in the torture complaints they filed against the officers responsible for their detention at National Security Agency facilities. EIPR also said the prosecution had not summoned or heard testimony from the officers named in the complaints or witnesses to the incidents. It also noted that the journalists had not claimed to have visible injuries but had reported being subjected to torture, ill-treatment, threats and physical and psychological coercion. The post State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: PM Shehbaz, EU official discuss Pakistan's efforts to curb migrant smuggling
items.description: ISLAMABAD: European Union Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday to discuss strengthening Pakistan-EU cooperation in migration and mobility, one of the eight pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan 2019. Welcoming Commissioner Brunner on his first visit to Pakistan, the prime minister underscored the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with the EU, according to a press release by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The premier highlighted Pakistan’s sustained efforts to curb irregular migration and combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking through legislative reforms, institutional strengthening, effective enforcement and international cooperation. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation across all pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan. PM Shehbaz emphasised that efforts to address irregular migration should be complemented by practical opportunities for safe, orderly and regular migration. He noted that expanding legal pathways for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals would help meet the labour market needs of European countries while reducing prospective migrants’ vulnerability to smuggling networks. Brunner appreciated the measures taken and cooperation extended by the government of Pakistan, the PMO said. He expressed confidence that these efforts would contribute to expanding legal migration pathways and promoting mutually beneficial labour mobility between Pakistan and the European Union. President Zardari calls for more legal migration opportunities Brunner also called on President Asif Ali Zardari at the President’s House today, according to a two-part statement issued by the official presidential account on social media. “The meeting focused on Pakistan-EU relations, cooperation on migration management, efforts to combat human trafficking and migrant smuggling, and opportunities to facilitate legal migration,” the statement said. President Zardari called for greater opportunities for legal migration for Pakistani workers and professionals in Europe. He emphasised that Pakistan’s sustained efforts to curb irregular migration should be matched by “expanded legal pathways, skills-based mobility and structured cooperation” with the EU. He said that Pakistan attached great importance to its cooperation with the EU and reaffirmed the country’s commitment to implementing the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan. The president highlighted the cooperation between the two countries in curbing irregular migration, noting that Pakistan continued to implement the EU Readmission Agreement and had readmitted more than 30,000 individuals over the years. He stressed the country’s commitment to combating human trafficking and irregular migration through “stronger legislation, institutional capacity, border controls and international cooperation”, the statement said. The president noted that, according to EU figures, irregular migration from Pakistan reduced by 64 per cent in the last 18 months, making it the only country in the region to achieve such a reduction. He said this progress reflected Pakistan’s “sustained efforts” and underlined the importance of expanding safe and legal avenues for migration. According to the president’s office, the meeting was informed that Pakistan had sought the EU’s assistance in strengthening the capacity of the Pakistan Coast Guards and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to enhance efforts to combat irregular migration and migrant smuggling. “The president emphasised that legal migration pathways are essential to providing safe opportunities for workers and reducing reliance on smuggling networks,” the statement added. He highlighted the Pakistan-EU Migration and Mobility Dialogue as a “useful framework for matching Pakistan’s human-resource potential with European labour-market needs”, and expressed the hope that the next round of dialogue — expected to take place in Brussels early next year — would advance this cooperation. He expressed the country’s readiness to work with the EU on a structured mechanism to match its workforce with European labour-market requirements. President Zardari also welcomed the expansion of the EU Talent Partnerships framework and called for greater opportunities for skilled workers and professionals, including through circular migration. He expressed the hope that, given this partnership and the country’s efforts to curb irregular migration, the EU would consider establishing a European Legal Gateway Office in Pakistan. He said Pakistan and the EU have a “broad-based relationship spanning political dialogue, trade, development cooperation and other areas of mutual interest”, the statement added. He expressed confidence that continued engagement would strengthen mutual understanding and help advance practical cooperation on migration and mobility. Commissioner Brunner appreciated Pakistan’s role in maintaining regional balance and said Pakistan has done an “amazing job” in this regard, the statement noted. He also commended Pakistan’s efforts to prevent irregular migrants from undertaking dangerous journeys that cost many of them their lives. The commissioner was accompanied by EU Ambassador to Pakistan Raimundas Karoblis; Director for Migration and Home Affairs of the European Commission Henrik Nielsen; and member of Brunner’s cabinet, Grigorios Delavekouras. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, Senator Sherry Rehman, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and former federal minister Naveed Qamar also attended the meeting, the statement added. Dar meets commissioner, highlights efforts to curb irregular migration The EU commissioner also met with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad, during which the deputy premier highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to curb irregular migration and combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking, the Foreign Office (FO) said. He stressed that these efforts should be complemented by greater opportunities for legal migration for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals. According to a statement issued by the FO, Dar expressed satisfaction with the positive momentum in Pakistan–EU relations. “The two sides discussed ways to strengthen cooperation on migration and mobility, a key pillar of the Pakistan–EU Strategic Engagement Plan (2019),” the FO said. It added that Brunner appreciated Pakistan’s progress in curbing irregular migration and noted the scope for expanding legal pathways for migration. Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its partnership with the EU. He expressed the hope that Brunner’s visit would lead to “practical outcomes that benefit both sides”, the statement added. Naqvi, EU commissioner discuss border security Separately, Brunner also met with Interior Minister Naqvi in Islamabad, where they discussed enhancing cooperation in border security, legal migration and border management. The meeting was followed by delegation-level talks. Brunner appreciated Pakistan’s measures against illegal migration, describing the 64pc reduction in illegal migration to Europe resulting from the country’s efforts as commendable. He said the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) had demonstrated professional competence despite limited resources, which was commendable. He added that the decline in illegal migration would pave the way for legal migration. Naqvi said Pakistan had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards illegal migration. “After a 64pc reduction in illegal migration, our next target is its complete elimination,” the interior minister said, describing illegal migration as a serious global issue. The two sides also discussed the promotion of legal migration and enhancing opportunities for skilled workers between Pakistan and the European Union. Both sides agreed to further strengthen cooperation in immigration, institutional coordination and border management, and to work together on the EU’s Eastern Corridor Initiative to eliminate illegal migration. They also discussed increasing mutual cooperation to enhance the capacity of Pakistan Coast Guards and agreed to increase collaboration to promote border security and legal migration. Brunner assured Pakistan of all possible cooperation in this regard. The meeting was attended by the interior secretary, special and additional interior secretaries, FIA director general, Federal Constabulary inspector general, NCCIA director general, passports director general, Islamabad chief commissioner and other officials. Last month, Naqvi said Pakistan had recorded a 64pc reduction in illegal migration to Europe, describing the achievement as challenging despite limited resources. He said Pakistan’s next target was to eliminate illegal migration completely, stressing the need to expand legal migration opportunities, adopt modern technology and strengthen institutional capacity. In February, Pakistan and three European countries — Italy, Spain and Greece — reached a consensus on promoting legal pathways to “effectively combat illegal migration”. The three countries endorsed Naqvi’s proposal to establish legal pathways as a strategy to combat illegal migration and human smuggling during a conference.

items.title: PTI's Ali Zafar terms governor's rule in KP 'political crisis disguised as security solution'; ministers defend move
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Treasury and opposition members in the Senate debated the governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Tuesday, with PTI’s Barrister Ali Zafar terming the development a “political crisis disguised as a security solution” while federal ministers defended the move. The Centre on Sunday imposed governor’s rule in KP and emergency in 12 of its districts, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The proclamations now require Parliament’s approval. It was against this backdrop that National Assembly and Senate sessions were convened on Tuesday. In the Senate, PTI’s Parliamentary Leader in the Senate Barrister Ali Zafar remarked that what was happening in KP was not merely an administrative decision but a “test of Pakistan’s Constitution”. “The Constitution must be our shield in a crisis, not a casualty of the crisis. The question is: are we using the Constitution to protect Pakistan, or are we using an emergency to change the political order of Pakistan?” he said. Zafar said no political party or patriotic Pakistani wanted terrorism to flourish and that terrorism must be defeated with full strength. “But we must defeat terrorism without allowing the fight against terrorism to become a fight against constitutional democracy,” he said. Referring to the constitutional provisions related to governor’s rule and emergency, he said Article 232 was to be employed in the situation of emergency and not as a “political weapon”. Similarly, Article 234 provided for extraordinary arrangements intended for extraordinary circumstances, he added. “Their existence does not mean they could be exercised without limits. The government must demonstrate that the constitutional conditions [for emergency and governor’s rule] have genuinely been met, that the action is necessary and proportionate, and that every applicable procedure has been followed. The existence of an emergency power does not place its exercise above the Constitution,” he said. Zafar further argued that the Centre could not simply declare that a provincial government could no longer function constitutionally and treat that declaration as the end argument. The legal basis, evidence, scope and consequences must withstand scrutiny, and courts must remain free to determine legality, he asserted. “If the government’s case is that terrorism has created an extraordinary situation in particular districts, it must explain why its response extended to the entire province and what safeguards protected the rest,” he added. The PTI alleged that “this is a political crisis disguised as a security solution”, pointing to the timing of the measure that came amid heightened political tensions and a breakdown of the dialogue between the government and the opposition, including the PTI, in the Centre. “You cannot restore public confidence by making people believe that their elected mandate can be taken away in the name of security,” he said. Zafar said the issue concerned provincial autonomy, federalism, elected representation, fundamental rights and the balance between the federation and its units. “Once extraordinary powers are normalised against one political opponent, no province and no party can assume it will never be the next one. Today it may be KP; tomorrow the precedent may be used elsewhere,” he warned. Calling on the Senate not to become a “rubber stamp”, he said Parliament, which represented the federation and gave every province an equal voice, must examine legal grounds, demand evidence and scrutinise necessity and proportionality for the measures in KP. “You may control the administration, but you cannot command democratic legitimacy. You may suspend a government, issue notifications and deploy the machinery of the state, but you cannot manufacture public trust by force. “If emergency is genuinely about protecting citizens, prove it through lawful, targeted and accountable action. If it becomes an instrument to suppress an elected mandate, the damage will outlast this government,” he said. Zafar added, “The Constitution is not an obstacle to national security; it is the foundation of national security. Break that foundation in the name of protecting Pakistan, and you may win control for a day but you will weaken the state for years to come.” Leader of the Opposition in Senate Raja Nasir Abbas termed Oct 11, when emergency and governor’s rule was imposed in KP, a “black day”, ruing celebrations by the “champions of democracy over the removal of a democratic government elected with two-thirds majority”. He maintained that an agreement between the Centre and the opposition had been reached on political issues, claiming that differences arose over linking security issues with political issues. He warned that “unnecessary violence” created hatred against the state among youth and urged the immediate withdrawal of the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency, as well as the resolution of issues through dialogue. Political matters could have been resolved by giving more time to negotiations, he added. Ministers defend governor’s rule For his part, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi maintained that imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in KP was not in violation of the Constitution. “The PML-N and PPP sat together and examined every clause to ensure that no provision was violated,” he said, adding that the decision was not an easy one. He said talks between the Centre and the opposition had focused on terrorism from the first day. The minister added that the Centre had contacted the PTI leadership, including party Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, on Oct 10, asking him to suggest amendments in the draft that was to be signed between the two sides after the talks. “Had an agreement been reached, this step would not have been taken,” he said. Naqvi said the government made six amendments in the draft, which was sent to KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who has become non-functional as the provincial chief executive following the imposition of governor’s rule. The interior minister alleged that Afridi forwarded the draft to PTI leader Murad Saeed, after which the matter was “sabotaged”. Referring to security situation in KP, he said law enforcement and security personnel were laying down their lives while the “chief minister was delivering speeches against them”. He alleged that some in the PTI were in “contact with the Taliban and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan”, adding that evidence of this would be presented when required. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also spoke in the House, saying that the federal cabinet had “rightly decided” last week to end the process of political reconciliation with the PTI. He stressed that the PPP and PML-N had both made efforts to reach a point of understanding with the PTI. Regarding arguments that terrorism was also prevalent in Balochistan while emergency and governor’s rule were only in KP, he highlighted that the Balochistan government was “fully on board” with the Centre in fighting terrorism. “Whatever has happened is according to the law and Constitution,” he contented. Parliament approval for governor’s rule President Asif Ali Zardari had on Sunday issued proclamations of emergency and governor’s rule under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, respectively. According to Article 232, in case the president “acts on his own” — which was not the case for KP as he acted on PM Shehbaz’s advice — the proclamation of emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days. It also empowers Parliament “to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during emergency. Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time”. In the upper house, Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulemai-i-Islam–Fazl (JUI-F) had submitted a resolution on Monday opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. NA session An NA session was also held on Tuesday, but concluded without any significant development. When the session began at around 7pm, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq administered the oath of membership to PML-N’s Malik Munir Iqbal Channar, who won the Bahawalpur polls last month held to fill the seat of his late father Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar. Lawmakers then offered prayers for late MNA Chaudhry Mahmood Bashir Virk, who died last month after a prolonged illness. As MNAs from various parties took their turns to recall the services of Virk, there was slight commotion, which prompted the speaker to urge PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan to respect the late MNA. Gohar remarked that sessions are usually adjourned after prayers for a deceased member. Referring to the governor’s rule in KP, he said the “funeral of this house was also held on Oct 11”. “We tried to give you very much in dialogue, but you (PTI) were not ready to take what we had offered,” the speaker replied, then switched off Gohar’s mic. The speaker said political discussion will not be allowed today, but tomorrow (Wednesday). PPP’s Syed Naveed Qamar also urged the PTI chairman to acknowledge the services of Virk, who had stood by the Constitution. He said the PTI could raise its issues later as well. Lawmakers then continued to pay tribute to Virk, with Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal among those who highlighted his professional life. The proceedings were then adjourned till 11am on Wednesday. PTI seeks production orders for 9 MNAs Earlier in the day, the PTI requested the NA speaker to issue production orders for its nine “detained” MNAs ahead of NA and Senate sessions on Tuesday. In a letter to NA Speaker Sadiq, Chief Whip Amir Dogar claimed that the nine MNAs were “currently detained” and requested him to issue production orders for them to enable them to attend the 30th session starting today. The lawmakers comprised Haji Imtiaz Ahmad Choudhry (ΝΑ-68), Muhammad Jamal Ahsan Khan (NA-89), Mian Ghous Muhammad (ΝΑ-170), Sanaullah Khan Mastikhel (NΑ-91), Dawar Khan Kundi (NA-43), Junaid Akbar (NA-09), Amjad Ali Khan (NA-02), Fazal Muhammad Khan (ΝΑ-25) and Adil Khan Bazai (NA-262). “As the speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan, the impartiality of your esteemed office requires that production orders be issued for all detained members, irrespective of their political affiliation, to ensure that no constituency remains unrepresented during the proceedings of the House,” the letter read. It requested Sadiq to issue the production orders under Rule 108 of the 2007 Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly.

items.title: 2027: INEC meets security agencies, party leaders, others in Lagos
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State on Tuesday met with security agencies, political parties and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and ensure peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections. Speaking at the stakeholders’ meeting in Lagos, Prof Ayobami Salami, Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), said the meeting also aimed at mobilising public support for effective implementation of the commission’s electoral plans. Salami said the commission was intensifying preparations in logistics, personnel deployment, election security, voter education and accessibility. He said INEC had moved from strategic planning to active operational implementation, with nine of the 14 scheduled milestones for the 2027 elections already accomplished as of Oct. 6. “At the national level, the Register of Voters currently stands at approximately 103 million. “Preparations are also advancing in critical areas, including the procurement and delivery of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, software upgrades, battery optimisation and biometric calibration. “Similarly, extensive logistical arrangements are being made for the deployment of over 100,000 vehicles and 4,000 boats nationwide,” he said. The REC added that recruitment of approximately 1.4 million election personnel through the INECPRES portal was ongoing, with the application window scheduled to close on Nov. 18. He said Lagos, with 7,488,633 registered voters, remained strategically important to the electoral process, requiring meticulous planning and coordinated deployment of resources across its 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs). According to him, the state has 245 Registration Areas and 13,325 Polling Units, making effective logistics and inter-agency cooperation essential to the successful conduct of the elections. Salami said the commission was taking account of Lagos’ peculiar challenges, including traffic congestion, densely populated communities, commercial activities, difficult-to-access settlements and riverine locations. “Beyond these figures are the distinctive operational realities of Lagos: a large and mobile population, densely populated urban communities, extensive commercial activities, traffic challenges, some difficult-to-access settlements and riverine locations. “These peculiarities demand careful planning and solutions tailored to the circumstances of individual communities. “Our commitment is to ensure that these challenges are anticipated and addressed through timely, coordinated and effective operational arrangements,” he said. He said preparations included transportation planning, timely deployment of election materials, activation of Registration Area Centres (RACs) and assessment of the readiness of election personnel and facilities. The REC added that INEC was strengthening internal coordination and monitoring mechanisms to identify potential operational challenges early and address them before they affected election activities. He said the commission would also provide assistive materials, including Braille ballot guides, EC30 PWD posters and magnifying glasses, where applicable, to promote participation by persons with disabilities. Salami urged organisations representing persons with disabilities to continue engaging with the commission and providing recommendations to improve accessibility and inclusion. On election security, he said INEC would continue working with relevant security agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), led by the Nigeria Police Force, to identify and mitigate potential electoral risks. “Our collective priority is to safeguard voters, election personnel, observers, electoral materials and facilities throughout the electoral process. “Particular attention will be given to prevention of electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying, ballot snatching and other unlawful activities capable of undermining the credibility of elections. “In collaboration with relevant law enforcement and anti-corruption agencies, appropriate preventive and enforcement measures will be pursued in accordance with the law,” he said. The REC called on political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their activities responsibly, respect electoral laws and avoid actions capable of disrupting public peace. He stressed that political competition should not be used to justify violence, intimidation or other unlawful conduct, adding that protecting citizens’ right to participate freely in elections was a shared responsibility. Salami also raised concerns about misinformation, disinformation and the misuse of artificial intelligence to circulate manipulated images, fabricated reports, synthetic audio and video recordings, deepfakes and voice clones. He urged political actors, media practitioners, civil society organisations and members of the public to verify election-related information through authorised INEC communication channels before sharing it. The REC reiterated that the collation and declaration of election results must follow established legal procedures and be undertaken only by duly authorised electoral officials. He said unverified figures and speculative reports should not be presented as official results, warning that false information could generate confusion, heighten political tensions and undermine public confidence in the electoral process. Salami emphasised that the successful conduct of the elections required the commitment of all stakeholders, noting that INEC could not achieve the objective of credible elections acting alone. “Political parties have a great responsibility to promote peaceful competition, respect electoral regulations and encourage responsible conduct among their members and supporters. “Security agencies must continue to provide a safe and enabling environment for electoral activities. “Traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, and community institutions remain important partners in promoting civic responsibility, peaceful coexistence and public participation,” he said. He also urged civil society organisations to intensify voter education and public enlightenment, while calling on the media to uphold accuracy, fairness and professionalism in reporting electoral activities. The REC appealed to stakeholders to encourage registered voters to verify their details on the Register of Voters, collect their Permanent Voter Cards, when available, and obtain electoral information from authorised sources. He said INEC remained committed to professionalism, transparency, inclusivity and effective implementation of its constitutional responsibilities as preparations for the 2027 General Elections gathered momentum. “Our objective is clear: to ensure that every stage of the electoral process is properly planned, effectively implemented and conducted in a manner that strengthens public confidence in the Commission and the integrity of elections. “With your continued cooperation, constructive engagement and shared commitment, I am confident that Lagos State can contribute significantly to the successful conduct of a peaceful, credible, transparent and inclusive General Elections,” he said. items.title: Personnes déplacées : les enfants reprennent l’école, les familles cherchent encore un toit
items.description: a Mopti, des familles deplacees ont quitte les salles de classe avant la rentree, permettant aux cours de reprendre. a Bamako, les enfants de l'ancien site de Faladie sont progressivement reinscrits dans les ecoles. Mais derriere cette reprise, les conditions de logement des familles restent preoccupantes. La rentree peut se poursuivre, mais le quotidien reste difficile pour de nombreuses familles deplacees. a Djenedaga et a Kouakrou, dans la region de Mopti, les familles qui occupaient des salles de classe ont rejoint de nouveaux lieux d'hebergement. a Bamako, celles de l'ancien site de Faladie se sont dispersees dans plusieurs quartiers, compliquant parfois la scolarisation des enfants. a Mopti, les ecoles respirent, les familles cherchent encore des abris a Djenedaga, les salles de classe ont ete liberees avant la rentree. Une solution rendue possible grâce a la mobilisation du chef du village, Boyon Karabenta, et de ses conseillers. Certaines familles ont trouve refuge dans des maisons abandonnees ou mises a leur disposition. Mais pour d'autres, l'hebergement reste provisoire. Le retour dans les localites d'origine dependra notamment de l'evolution de la situation securitaire. En attendant, les familles doivent s'adapter a leurs nouvelles conditions de vie. Boubacar Thienta, porte-parole des deplaces, souligne que « le site initialement propose a Medina Coura ne repond pas a leurs besoins ». Principalement issus de la communaute bozo, ces deplaces souhaitent etre heberges pres du fleuve, essentiel a leurs activites et a leur mode de vie. a Bamako, les enfants retrouvent progressivement le chemin de l'ecole Depuis la dispersion de l'ancien site de Faladie, les familles se sont installees dans plusieurs quartiers peripheriques, notamment a Sirakoro et a Mountougoula. Pour les parents, il faut desormais trouver une ecole accessible a leurs enfants, parfois loin de leur nouveau domicile. Malgre ces contraintes, les inscriptions avancent. Selon Amadou Tamboura, enseignant volontaire, la grande majorite des enfants a deja ete inscrite ou fait l'objet de demarches. Les parents peuvent s'orienter vers differents etablissements : ecoles classiques, medersas, ecoles franco-arabes ou privees. Mais inscrire un enfant ne suffit pas toujours a garantir sa presence reguliere en classe. Le logement, les deplacements et les depenses du quotidien restent des obstacles pour ces familles. Au-dela de la rentree, le defi de la continuite scolaire La liberation des salles de classe a Mopti et les reinscriptions a Bamako permettent aux enfants de poursuivre leur scolarite. Mais pour les familles deplacees, une autre urgence demeure : trouver un hebergement adapte et stable. La rentree est donc une etape franchie, pas la fin des difficultes. Pour eviter de nouvelles interruptions scolaires, les enfants auront besoin de conditions de vie qui leur permettent de rester durablement a l'ecole. items.title: Oil spill: Delta govt commences medical outreach in Odidi Federated communities
items.description: THE Delta State Government has commenced an emergency free comprehensive medical and surgical outreach to residents of Odidi Federated Communities along the Trans-Forcados Pipeline in Warri South-West Local Government Area, following the oil spill that has affected the communities. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Joseph Onojaeme, who led the medical team, said the initiative was in compliance with the directive Governor Sheriff Oborevwori. He noted that the outreach would carry out multidisciplinary interventions, including surgeries, eye checks, dental care, laboratory investigations, medical outpatient care and others. The Commissioner commended the people of Odidi Federated Communities for the peaceful manner they had conducted themselves since the oil spill occurred. He appealed to residents to cooperate with the medical team, stressing that all drugs, mosquito nets and treatments being administered were completely free. Onojaeme highlighted the Governor’s keen interest in the well-being of Deltans, which said, had led to the construction and renovation of primary health care facilities across the state, as well as increased funding for these facilities. He assured that the government would continue to ensure that healthcare is easily accessible to all Deltans. Speaking on behalf of the Odidi Federated Communities, a community leader, Mr. Faith Mamamu, commended the Delta State Government for its prompt response to the oil spill crisis, which he said has disrupted the economic life of the communities. He said the people of Odidi were deeply grateful for the Governor’s concern and swift intervention. Beneficiaries of the outreach who spoke also commended Governor Oborevwori for his prompt response and for the free drugs and care provided to them, expressing appreciation that the government had come to their aid at a difficult time. Recall that Governor Oborevwori, on October 6, 2026, directed the Commissioner for Health to immediately deploy medical personnel to the affected communities to assess residents and determine the health implications of the pollution. items.title: Almamy Doukouré rend hommage à Sidya Touré : « la Guinée perd un grand serviteur de l’État »
items.description: Pour un devoir républicain, je me sens dans l’obligation morale, intellectuelle et religieuse de rendre un vibrant hommage à l’homme politique et d’État que fut l’ancien Premier ministre Sidya Touré. Je garde tout d’abord le souvenir d’un homme politique nommé à la tête du gouvernement par le président Lansana Conté, à une époque où la Guinée, à l’instar de nombreux pays africains, traversait une période de difficultés économiques marquée notamment par une forte inflation et la hausse des prix des biens et services. Dès sa nomination en 1996, Sidya Touré a engagé des réformes économiques et administratives destinées à redresser les finances publiques et à améliorer les conditions de vie des Guinéens. Sa volonté de réduire le train de vie de l’État, de limiter les dépenses superflues et de promouvoir une gestion rigoureuse des deniers publics est restée gravée dans ma mémoire, malgré mon jeune âge à l’époque. Je me souviens notamment de cette anecdote, rapportée à propos de ses rapports avec le président Lansana Conté, selon laquelle il aurait suggéré que le chef de l’État lui-même dispose d’un bulletin de paie pour sa fonction présidentielle et justifie ses notes de frais. Au-delà de l’ironie de cette remarque, j’y voyais l’expression d’une exigence fondamentale : nul ne devrait être au-dessus des règles de bonne gestion des ressources publiques. C’est ainsi que j’ai commencé à admirer cet homme d’État, dont la rigueur et le sens des responsabilités semblaient traduire une véritable volonté de servir la nation. C’est donc avec une grande fierté que j’avais accueilli sa nomination à la tête du gouvernement. Sa rigueur, son sens du devoir et son engagement en faveur de la bonne gouvernance constituaient, à mes yeux, des atouts majeurs pour conduire les réformes dont notre pays avait besoin. Ne pas lui rendre hommage aujourd’hui serait, à mon sens, faire preuve de malhonnêteté intellectuelle. Car rendre hommage à un homme d’État qui a consacré une partie importante de sa vie au service de sa nation, c’est reconnaître la valeur de son engagement en faveur de l’intérêt général. C’est aussi saluer un parcours marqué par le sens du devoir, le dévouement à la patrie et la volonté de contribuer au progrès de la Guinée. Un homme d’État ne se mesure pas uniquement aux fonctions qu’il a occupées, mais surtout aux actions qu’il a entreprises, aux sacrifices qu’il a consentis et à l’héritage qu’il laisse à son peuple. Aujourd’hui, la Guinée perd un grand serviteur de l’État. Au-delà des divergences et des clivages politiques, Sidya Touré incarnait, à mes yeux, une certaine conception de la vie publique, fondée sur la rigueur, le sens des responsabilités et l’attachement à l’intérêt national. Je considère qu’un hommage national devrait lui être rendu afin de saluer sa mémoire et son parcours au service de la Guinée. Son passage à la tête du gouvernement a marqué une période importante de notre histoire politique et économique. Son héritage mérite d’être évoqué avec objectivité, au-delà des appartenances partisanes, pour que les générations présentes et futures puissent en tirer les enseignements utiles. Je tiens également à exprimer ma reconnaissance aux autorités ivoiriennes, au peuple ivoirien ainsi qu’aux Guinéens de la diaspora, dans les différents pays, qui se sont mobilisés pour accompagner le défunt dans sa dernière demeure. Ces marques de solidarité et de fraternité témoignent de l’estime portée à sa personne et de l’importance des liens qui unissent nos peuples. J’adresse mes condoléances les plus attristées à sa famille biologique, à sa famille politique, à ses proches, à ses anciens collaborateurs ainsi qu’à l’ensemble du peuple de Guinée. Qu’Allah, le Tout-Puissant, lui accorde Son pardon et l’accueille dans Son paradis éternel. Amen. Almamy DOUKOURÉ Paris, France L’article Almamy Doukouré rend hommage à Sidya Touré : « la Guinée perd un grand serviteur de l’État » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: El Rey, en Ceuta: “La soberanía y la integridad territorial no son negociables y, ante cualquier riesgo, nuestra obligación es su defensa”
items.description: A última hora de la tarde de este martes, tras darse un baño de cariño y afecto por distintos puntos de la urbe de Ceuta, Felipe VI ha culminado su primera visita a la ciudad autónoma con un discurso muy contundente. Dentro del hotel Parador, el Rey ha calificado de “violación de nuestra frontera” el cruce multitudinario de finales de julio, ha defendido la “soberanía” y “la integridad” de la ciudad, y ha subrayado la “obligación” de defenderlas. Todo dos meses y medio después de la entrada masiva que ha puesto en jaque a la urbe africana. El monarca ha reivindicado además su papel como “jefe del Estado”, algo que no suele hacer en este tipo de alocuciones, y ha mantenido que “la violación de nuestra frontera sigue teniendo un enorme impacto en España entera”. “No os vamos a dejar solos ni indefensos”, ha prometido a los ceutíes, después de que miles de vecinos se acercaran a saludarle por las calles donde ha transcurrido el viaje . items.title: Automobile : le marché algérien atténue la baisse des ventes de Stellantis
items.description: L'alliance Stellantis qui est présente en Algérie avec sa marque Fiat, qui regroupe 14 marques automobiles, a publié les chiffres estimatifs de ses facturations du troisième trimestre 2026. Le groupe automobile franco-italo-américain fait état d’une hausse des facturations en Algérie qui permet d'atténuer la baisse globale estimée à 1% en glissement annuel. Stellantis, 1,3 millions de voitures facturées en un trimestre Stellantis est présent en Algérie à travers l’usine de la marque Fiat ouverte à Oran en 2023. Selon les chiffres publiés, Stellantis a facturé dans le monde 1,3 millions d’unités au troisième trimestre 2026. Il est expliqué sur le site internet de l'alliance franco-italo-américaine que le terme “facturations” désigne “le volume de véhicules livrés aux concessionnaires, aux distributeurs ou directement par l’entreprise à des clients particuliers et professionnels, ce qui, généralement, permet de comptabiliser le chiffre d’affaires”. Le nombre de facturations par rapport à la même période de 2025 a diminué presque dans toutes les zones géographiques, hormis en “Europe élargie” où il a augmenté de 54 000 unités, soit 10 % de plus en glissement annuel. Il a en revanche baissé de 12% en Amérique du Nord, avec 47 000 unités de moins, principalement en raison des arrêts de production planifiés. Des baisses sont aussi enregistrées en Amérique du Sud (avec notamment une progression de 13 000 unités au Brésil et un recul de 11 000 unités en Argentine), et en Asie-Pacifique. Les ventes en Algérie ont compensé la baisse mondiale Au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique, le recul est de 21%, soit d’environ 20 000 unités. Les marques de l’alliance ont réalisé des performances opposées d’un pays à un autre. En Turquie, la baisse est d’environ 21 000 unités “dans un contexte de marché moins favorable”. En revanche, les résultats sont plus que bons en Algérie. Sans livrer de chiffres, Stellantis a indiqué que la hausse des facturations en Algérie et au Maroc a “plus que compensé la baisse des volumes dans les pays du Conseil de Coopération du Golfe, affectés par le conflit régional.” S’agissant des performances par marque en Europe, Stellantis cite les Citroën C3 et C3 Aircross, Opel/Vauxhall Frontera et Fiat Grande Panda, qui ont représenté environ 26 000 unités supplémentaires. Les nouvelles Fiat 500 Hybrid et Jeep Compass ont également contribué à hauteur d’environ 6 000 unités et 5 000 unités supplémentaires. Stellantis note en revanche une baisse d’environ 28 000 unités des facturations d’autres modèles, notamment les Opel Corsa, Opel Mokka, Citroën C4, Alfa Romeo Junior et Peugeot 2008.
